tldr: HqcLethe streams HQC (code-based KEM) encapsulation in packet-sized pieces using CRT-split polynomial multiplication, enabling stateless post-quantum key exchange on memory-constrained servers.
motivation: Stateless post-quantum handshakes such as post-quantum WireGuard need cryptographic diversity, but HQC keys are too large for a single packet and buffering multi-packet handshakes reintroduces memory-exhaustion attack surface. McTiny showed streaming works for Classic McEliece, but HQC's cyclic polynomial multiplication is non-local and does not split easily.
method: The encapsulation's polynomial multiplication is decomposed into independent Chinese-remainder-theorem remainders, one per packet, and masked so each packet reveals no more than an ordinary HQC ciphertext; security is proved in Rocq/SSProve and session secrecy, server authentication and forward secrecy in ProVerif, with client puzzles bounding CPU exhaustion.
result: On a Raspberry Pi 3B+ each worker runs in a fixed 1.2–1.6 MiB, and at category 5 the scheme sends 27x fewer bytes and uses 9.0x less server CPU than McTiny.
conclusion: Streaming CRT-based encapsulation makes code-based KEMs viable for stateless, memory-limited servers while preserving security guarantees and eliminating the memory-exhaustion vector.

title: They Will See Johnny's Message: A Measurement Study Of Post-Quantum Cryptography Across Email Delivery Paths
authors: Jaehwan Park, Sunghyun Park, Kevin Nam, Doowon Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Harvest-now, decrypt-later (HNDL) attacks make the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) urgent for email. This paper presents a systematic measurement that jointly examines PQC deployment across email service stages, negotiation by communicating peers, and usable message encryption. Endpoint-level support alone does not establish PQC readiness across email workflows because submission, relay, and access use independently negotiated Transport Layer Security (TLS) connections. We therefore combine three snapshots of relay, submission, access, and webmail services associated with the Tranco Top~1M domains with controlled tests of mail clients, sending servers, and OpenPGP and S/MIME implementations. Our measurements reveal a transition concentrated among a few providers, with available capability not consistently translating into actual use. Fewer than half of the domains in each service panel support PQC, and Google alone accounts for approximately 87\% of hybrid-capable relay domains. Only two of eight tested sending providers negotiate PQC with our receiver, although five accept it inbound. When TLS groups are restricted to PQC, four of the six incompatible senders fall back to plaintext where unencrypted SMTP remains permitted. At the message layer, limited native key generation, key-format incompatibilities, and backend integration failures further constrain usable PQC encryption.
tldr: A large-scale measurement study of how post-quantum cryptography is deployed and actually negotiated across email delivery paths (submission, relay, access, webmail) and message-level encryption (OpenPGP/S/MIME).
motivation: Harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks make the migration of email to post-quantum cryptography urgent, but endpoint-level PQC support alone does not guarantee that PQC is used end-to-end across the independently negotiated TLS connections in an email workflow.
method: The authors combine three snapshots of relay, submission, access, and webmail services for Tranco Top-1M domains with controlled tests of mail clients, sending servers, and OpenPGP/S/MIME implementations, including experiments where TLS groups are restricted to PQC.
result: Fewer than half of domains in each service panel support PQC, Google accounts for ~87% of hybrid-capable relay domains, only two of eight sending providers negotiate PQC with the test receiver, and four of six incompatible senders fall back to plaintext when PQC-only groups are enforced; message-layer key generation, key-format incompatibility, and backend integration failures further limit usable PQC email encryption.
conclusion: PQC readiness for email is concentrated among a few providers and available capability frequently does not translate into actual use, so real end-to-end post-quantum email encryption remains far from deployment.

title: The Exact Weight Spectrum Of $\RM(m-7,m$): A Counterexample To The Carlet-Sol\'{e} Conjecture
authors: Qichun Wang Yueying Lou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boolean functions are widely used in cryptography and coding theory. A key challenge lies in finding the weight spectrum for all [MATH]-variable Boolean functions of degree at most [MATH], also known as the Reed--Muller code [MATH]. In 2023, Carlet and Sol\'{e} determined the weight spectra of [MATH] for [MATH], and conjectured the weight spectrum of [MATH]) for [MATH]. The weight spectra of [MATH] and [MATH] were determined by Carlet in 2024 and by Lou and Wang in 2025, respectively, confirming the Carlet-Sol\'{e} conjecture for the cases [MATH]. Very recently, Leuenberger et al. and Wei et al. investigated the weight spectrum of [MATH] independently, and there are eight potential weights which have not been determined. Up until now, the weight spectra of the Reed--Muller codes [MATH] are still unknown for [MATH]. In this paper, we determine the exact weight spectrum of [MATH] for every [MATH]. By combining affine geometry and Fourier analysis, we exclude the conjectured eight weights for [MATH]. We then extend the exclusions to all higher dimensions using a geometric transfer. Consequently, we provide a counterexample to the Carlet-Sol\'{e} conjecture.
tldr: The paper determines the exact weight spectrum of the Reed-Muller code RM(m-7,m) for all m, disproving the 2023 Carlet-Solé conjecture by excluding eight previously conjectured weights.
motivation: Weight spectra of Reed-Muller codes RM(r,m) remain unknown for small co-dimensions, and the Carlet-Solé conjecture predicted eight additional weights for RM(m-7,m); resolving this is a central open problem in classical coding theory and Boolean function analysis.
method: The authors combine affine geometry with Fourier analysis of Boolean functions to exclude the eight conjectured weights in a base case, then propagate the exclusions to all higher dimensions via a geometric transfer argument.
result: The exact weight spectrum of RM(m-7,m) is obtained for every m, and the eight weights predicted by the Carlet-Solé conjecture are shown not to occur, yielding an explicit counterexample.
conclusion: The Carlet-Solé conjecture is false; the work completes the weight-spectrum determination for co-dimension seven and illustrates geometric/Fourier techniques for Reed-Muller weight enumeration.

title: Variable-Length Feedback Coding With Universal Decoding And Bandit Channel Selection
authors: Recep Can Yavas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study variable-length feedback (VLF) coding over [MATH] additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels whose noise variances are unknown to both terminals but lie in a known interval. The receiver selects one channel at each time, conveys the selection over noiseless feedback, and must learn the channel qualities while decoding, to avoid overusing suboptimal channels. This setting, which we call the VLF-Bandit problem, combines VLF coding, universal decoding, and bandit channel selection. We develop two joint coding and channel-selection schemes. The VLSF-Bandit scheme is a single-phase variable-length stop-feedback (VLSF) scheme based on a Gaussian random codebook, a score formed from a ratio of likelihood mixtures, and the asymptotically optimal [MATH] bandit algorithm applied to the received power. The VLF-Bandit scheme sends the message in packets by Schalkwijk--Kailath transmission, uses its normalized outputs as noise samples to learn the variances, and lets its exploration packets carry message bits. We prove second-order achievability bounds for both schemes, which are first-order optimal. In the logarithm of the achievable codebook size, the magnitude of the [MATH] coefficient, with [MATH] the average decoding time, is a baseline of one plus a channel-exploration term for VLSF-Bandit. For VLF-Bandit, this magnitude is smaller, with a universal-decoding term replacing the baseline and a smaller channel-exploration term. The VLF-Bandit bound improves on the universal VLF bound of Yavas and Tan (2025) for [MATH] and on the bound of an explore-then-commit strategy whenever [MATH].
tldr: The paper introduces the VLF-Bandit problem, which combines variable-length feedback coding, universal decoding, and bandit-based channel selection over AWGN channels with unknown noise variances, and proposes two joint coding and selection schemes with second-order achievability bounds.
motivation: In settings where noise variances of multiple parallel AWGN channels are unknown to both terminals, the receiver must simultaneously learn channel qualities and decode, so naive use of suboptimal channels wastes resources; classical VLF coding theory provides no guidance for this exploration-exploitation tradeoff.
method: The VLSF-Bandit scheme uses a Gaussian random codebook, a score built from a ratio of likelihood mixtures, and an asymptotically optimal UCB-type bandit algorithm on received power; the VLF-Bandit scheme transmits via Schalkwijk-Kailath packets, treats normalized outputs as noise samples for variance learning, and embeds message bits in exploration packets.
result: Second-order achievability bounds are proven for both schemes, both first-order optimal; the VLF scheme attains a smaller backoff coefficient than the VLSF scheme, improving on the universal VLF bound of Yavas and Tan (2025) and on explore-then-commit strategies in a specified regime.
conclusion: Joint coding and channel-selection design yields tighter finite-blocklength achievability for unknown-variance multi-channel VLF communication, with exploration costs quantified explicitly.

title: PDE-Based Bounds On Optimal Exponents In Active Simple Hypothesis Testing
authors: Himadri Mandal Sushant Vijayan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present general upper and lower bounds on the optimal error exponent for the Active Simple Hypothesis Testing (ASHT) problem. ASHT has been extensively studied across diverse fields including Information Theory, Bandits, and Operations Research, a precise characterization of this optimal exponent has remained elusive. This work combines a recent Partial Differential Equation (PDE) characterization of the optimal exponent by Vijayan (2025) with the comparison principle of viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi PDEs. This leads to bounds that are parametrized by convex functions, sets and lower Hamiltonian relaxations, a flexibility that generalizes many known results in the literature.
tldr: The paper derives general PDE-based upper and lower bounds on the optimal error exponent for Active Simple Hypothesis Testing.
motivation: Active Simple Hypothesis Testing has been studied across information theory, bandits, and operations research, but a precise characterization of its optimal error exponent has remained elusive.
method: It combines a recent PDE characterization of the optimal exponent with the comparison principle for viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi PDEs to obtain bounds parametrized by convex functions, sets, and lower Hamiltonian relaxations.
result: The resulting bounds are flexible and generalize many known results in the literature on active hypothesis testing.
conclusion: The work advances classical information-theoretic hypothesis testing via PDE methods, but it has no direct quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems component.

title: Experimental Geometric State Preparation On The Bloch Sphere Via Linear Mechanical Resonator
authors: Abrar N-E Faiaz, Donte Mcmullen, Kazi T Mahmood, M. Arif Hasan, Pierre Deymier, Keith Runge, Joshua A. Levine
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Bloch sphere representation, familiar from quantum two-level systems, can also describe classical linear systems whose dynamics are effectively confined to two modes. Here, we experimentally realize this framework in a linear two-mass, three-spring mechanical system by controlling superpositions of its symmetric and antisymmetric eigenmodes. The system is driven from both boundaries at a fixed frequency between the two resonances, so that the steady-state response remains within a two-mode manifold. By independently varying the relative amplitude and phase of the boundary excitations, we generate tunable modal superpositions. Scanning laser vibrometer measurements and frequency-domain analysis are used to extract the complex modal coefficients, which are then normalized and mapped onto Bloch sphere coordinates. This reconstruction reveals planar rotations of the state under phase sweeps and continuous steering between eigenstates under amplitude-ratio tuning. These results provide an experimental validation of Bloch sphere state reconstruction and steady-state geometric state preparation in a minimal linear mass-spring platform, establishing a simple classical testbed for exploring two-mode manifold dynamics.
tldr: A classical two-mass, three-spring mechanical resonator is driven to emulate Bloch-sphere state preparation and geometric steering between two effective modes.
motivation: The Bloch sphere, originally a representation for quantum two-level systems, also describes classical linear systems restricted to a two-mode manifold; the authors seek a simple experimental testbed for such dynamics.
method: The mechanical system is driven at both boundaries at a frequency between the two resonances, keeping the steady state in a two-mode manifold; relative amplitude and phase of the excitations are varied, and scanning laser vibrometry plus frequency-domain analysis extract normalized complex modal coefficients mapped to Bloch coordinates.
result: Phase sweeps produce planar rotations of the reconstructed state, and amplitude-ratio tuning yields continuous steering between the symmetric and antisymmetric eigenmodes, validating Bloch-sphere state reconstruction.
conclusion: The work establishes a minimal classical mass-spring platform for two-mode geometric state preparation, offered as a classical analogue rather than a quantum device.

title: Quantum State Preparation For Complex-Valued Amplitudes
authors: Fred Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a state preparation procedure that takes binary registers containing the real and imaginary parts of a complex number [MATH] and prepares an amplitude approximating [MATH], where [MATH] is a normalization constant. The magnitude and argument are computed using the Coordinate Rotation Digital Computer (CORDIC) algorithm. We then encode the magnitude into an amplitude, and apply phase gates to introduce the argument. A reversible in-place multiplier allows the coordinate updates to use fixed precision while clearing their temporary workspace. The procedure uses [MATH] [MATH] gates and [MATH] additional qubits. Compared with separately encoding the real and imaginary parts and combining them through LCU, the construction can allow a smaller normalization and reduce amplitude-amplification costs. The computed polar representation also remains available for further arithmetic before amplitude-encoding.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum state-preparation procedure for encoding complex amplitudes using CORDIC-based polar conversion, amplitude encoding, and phase gates.
motivation: It aims to efficiently prepare normalized complex amplitudes from binary registers representing real and imaginary parts, avoiding separate LCU-style encoding of real and imaginary components.
method: The method computes magnitude and argument via the CORDIC algorithm, encodes the magnitude into a qubit amplitude, applies phase gates for the argument, and uses a reversible in-place multiplier to clear temporary workspace at fixed precision.
result: The construction uses a stated number of gates and additional qubits and can yield a smaller normalization constant and reduced amplitude-amplification cost compared with separately encoding real and imaginary parts and combining via LCU.
conclusion: The polar representation remains available for further arithmetic before amplitude encoding, making the procedure potentially useful as a quantum arithmetic/state-preparation primitive.

title: Propagation Estimates For The Many-body Boson Star Equation
authors: S\'ebastien Breteaux, Charlotte Dietze, J\'er\'emy Faupin, Viviana Grasselli, Jinyeop Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the many-body boson star equation in the mean-field regime. Under a decay assumption on the solution to the effective one-body equation, we prove a uniform-in-time trace-norm estimate comparing the one-particle reduced density matrix of the many-body state with the projection onto the one-body solution. This establishes uniform-in-time mean-field convergence as the particle number goes to infinity. Furthermore, for the many-body dynamics, we establish both a maximal velocity bound, which can be seen as a Lieb--Robinson-type bound, and a minimal velocity bound. As an application, we recover maximal and minimal velocity bounds for the one-body boson star equation by passing to the mean-field limit.
tldr: The paper proves uniform-in-time mean-field convergence and velocity bounds for the many-body boson star equation.
motivation: The authors study the mean-field limit of the many-body boson star equation and seek quantitative control over the convergence of the reduced density matrix to the effective one-body solution.
method: Under a decay assumption on the one-body solution, they derive a uniform-in-time trace-norm estimate comparing the one-particle reduced density matrix with the projection onto the one-body solution, and establish maximal and minimal velocity bounds.
result: They obtain uniform-in-time mean-field convergence as the particle number tends to infinity, along with a Lieb-Robinson-type maximal velocity bound and a minimal velocity bound for the many-body dynamics; these also yield velocity bounds for the one-body equation via the mean-field limit.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous propagation estimates for a nonlinear many-body boson star model, but it is a mathematical PDE/mean-field analysis rather than a contribution to the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems directions.

title: Effective Noise Thresholds For Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm Under Noisy Environment
authors: Yozef Tjandra, Hendrik Santoso Sugiarto, Celine Vania Setiadi, Joanna Gracia Tan, Andriyan Bayu Suksmono
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational quantum algorithms are leading candidates for practical utilisation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processors, but accumulating noise bounds the usefulness of circuit depths. For the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA), this trade-off has mostly been addressed by searching for the best depth for a given device. In this work, we consider the inverse question: how much noise each depth can tolerate. Using GPU-accelerated noisy QAOA simulations for MaxCut on three graph families with 6 to 18 vertices, depths up to 10 and three noise channels, we fit the approximation ratios with a generalised logistic surface. We propose the effective noise threshold as the inflection boundary of the logistic surfaces, a noise boundary separating reliable and unreliable QAOA approximation regimes. In general, the threshold decreases as depth rises, indicating that deeper circuits demand for stricter noise requirement for reliable approximation. Its best and worst values over depth divide the noise axis into three regions: every depth remains effective, depth must be chosen with care, or no depth induces effective optimisation. Assessing on the ibm_marrakesh processor, although modelled gate errors understate factual noise, the threshold modeling remains beneficial in informing qualitative depth-dependence structure and identifying dominating noise channel in noisy QAOA.
tldr: The paper defines effective noise thresholds for QAOA by fitting approximation-ratio surfaces under simulated noise and evaluating depth-dependent reliability.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms such as QAOA are limited by noise accumulation at increasing circuit depths, and practitioners need guidance on how much noise each depth can tolerate.
method: The authors perform GPU-accelerated noisy QAOA simulations for MaxCut on three graph families with 6–18 vertices, depths up to 10, and three noise channels, then fit generalized logistic surfaces to approximation ratios.
result: They identify effective noise thresholds as inflection boundaries of the fitted surfaces, find that thresholds generally decrease with depth, and use these boundaries to classify noise regimes where all, some, or no depths remain reliable.
conclusion: Effective noise thresholds provide a depth-dependent reliability analysis for QAOA under noise, with potential qualitative guidance for hardware such as ibm_marrakesh, though modeled gate errors understate actual device noise.

title: Theoretical Study Of High-order Harmonic Generation In Solids Based On Deep-learning Methods
authors: Wen-Feng Huang, Jia-Qi Liu, Xue-Bin Bian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids provides a compact and coherent EUV radiation, which has attracted considerable attention. Many theoretical methods for laser-crystal interactions are developed. However, an approach to treat large-scale amorphous systems with ab-initio accuracy is still lacking because of the enormous computational cost. Here, we incorporate molecular dynamics and tight-binding electron Hamiltonians based on deep-learning methods to solve the problem efficiently. Its accuracy is validated by comparing the HHG spectra of monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with those obtained using existing methods. Then we use it to study the temperature-dependent HHG in bulk Si. We uncover a distinct harmonic-order-dependent thermal response: low-order harmonics are enhanced with increasing temperature, whereas high-order harmonics are suppressed. The former is caused by the modification of the inter-site hopping in the system, while the latter is mainly influenced by the structural disorder induced by the thermal effects, in agreement with experimental observations. This work establishes a scalable computational strategy for investigating HHG in solids and provides new insights into the interplay between lattice fluctuations and ultrafast electron dynamics.
tldr: The authors combine deep-learning-based tight-binding Hamiltonians with molecular dynamics to simulate high-order harmonic generation in large-scale amorphous solids, applying the method to temperature-dependent HHG in bulk silicon.
motivation: Ab-initio treatment of laser-crystal interactions in large-scale disordered systems is prohibitively expensive, so a scalable yet accurate computational approach is needed to study HHG in solids.
method: Deep-learning surrogate models for tight-binding electron Hamiltonians are coupled to molecular dynamics, validated against monolayer h-BN HHG spectra and then applied to bulk Si at finite temperature.
result: A harmonic-order-dependent thermal response is found: low-order harmonics are enhanced with temperature (via modified inter-site hopping) while high-order harmonics are suppressed (via thermal structural disorder), matching experiments.
conclusion: The work offers a scalable computational strategy for HHG in solids and clarifies how lattice fluctuations shape ultrafast electron dynamics.

title: Parameter-Decoupled Superresolution With Airy-Disk-Informed Learning: Application To Ngc 4486b
authors: James Qu, Isabella L. Lee, Gang Zhang, Abdelali Sajia, Yashashree Jadhav, Xiao-Feng Qian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimating the separation of two unresolved or nearly unresolved sources from recorded intensity images is difficult when source brightness, mutual coherence, and phase are unknown and the point-spread function (PSF) departs from a Gaussian. We formulate Hermite--Gaussian (HG) projections of one- and two-dimensional Airy amplitudes and prove that ratios of mode probabilities with equal longitudinal parity exactly cancel the brightness, coherence, and phase nuisance parameters under a symmetric two-source model. For a one-dimensional Airy slice we achieve an explicit multi-ratio separation inversion. For the physical two-dimensional circular-pupil PSF we obtain exact finite-pupil overlap integrals and locally invertible separation responses. Motivated by these analytical invariants, we examine Airy-informed convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on synthetic Airy images with known separations. At 150,000 training images, the approximate mean absolute errors are 0.018 in plotted separation units, 10 times better comparing to 0.18 for non-Airy Gaussian PSF approximation. Applied to an archival Hubble Space Telescope image of the double nucleus of NGC 4486B, the Airy-informed CNN gives estimates of approximately 9.6--12.0 pc for training sets of 100,000--150,000 images, broadly consistent with the historical approximately 12 pc value. We distinguish exact optical-mode nuisance cancellation from empirical robustness of an image-only learned estimator and identify the limits imposed by PSF mismatch and extended galaxy structure.
tldr: The authors derive Hermite-Gaussian mode-probability ratio invariants for Airy-disk point-spread functions that cancel unknown source brightness, coherence and phase, and use them to motivate an Airy-informed CNN that estimates two-source separations, applying it to the double nucleus of NGC 4486B.
motivation: Separating two nearly unresolved sources from intensity images is ill-posed when brightness, mutual coherence, phase and PSF shape are unknown, and a Gaussian PSF approximation biases such estimates.
method: Analytical Hermite-Gaussian projections of 1D and 2D Airy amplitudes yield mode-probability ratios of equal longitudinal parity that are nuisance-parameter free, plus exact finite-pupil overlap integrals; these motivate training Airy-informed CNNs on synthetic images with known separations.
result: At 150,000 training images the CNN reaches a mean absolute error of about 0.018 separation units versus 0.18 for a Gaussian-PSF baseline, and applied to archival Hubble data it gives 9.6-12.0 pc for the NGC 4486B double nucleus, consistent with the historical ~12 pc.
conclusion: Exact optical-mode nuisance cancellation is distinguished from empirical robustness of an image-only learned estimator, with PSF mismatch and extended galaxy structure identified as the dominant limitations.

title: Universal Critical Jump For Inverse-Square Ising Ferromagnets
authors: Dyuman Bhattacharya
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every translation-invariant ferromagnetic Ising chain with [MATH], we prove [MATH], without restrictions on the finite core or the tail convergence rate. The proof bounds the energy of macroscopic interfaces and rules them out if the critical product exceeds one. Despite the nonzero jump, connected susceptibility is infinite both at criticality and in a neighboring ordered interval. At the critical coupling, the excess magnetization decays more slowly than any positive power of the field as the field tends to zero. We also prove the jump relation in continuous time, for a positive-Stieltjes class of Ohmic spin-boson models.
tldr: The paper proves a universal critical magnetization jump for translation-invariant inverse-square Ising ferromagnetic chains and extends the jump relation to continuous-time Ohmic spin-boson models.
motivation: The work aims to establish rigorous critical behavior for long-range Ising chains without restrictive assumptions on the finite core or tail convergence, and to connect this to certain spin-boson models.
method: The proof bounds the energy of macroscopic interfaces and rules them out when the critical product exceeds one, yielding the critical jump; a parallel argument is developed in continuous time for a positive-Stieltjes class of Ohmic spin-boson models.
result: A universal critical jump is proven, connected susceptibility is shown to be infinite at criticality and in a neighboring ordered interval, and the excess magnetization decays slower than any positive power of the field at critical coupling.
conclusion: The paper provides rigorous mathematical results on critical phenomena in inverse-square Ising ferromagnets and related spin-boson models, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anomalous Structures Of Fisher Zero Lines In Biorthogonal Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Wen-Hui Nie, Chong Li, Lin-Cheng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fisher zero lines of the Loschmidt amplitude in non-Hermitian quenches can exhibit anomalous structures in the complex time plane, such as divergence, separation, and the restriction of all branches or a specific branch to the real or imaginary axis. Here, we use the biorthogonal framework to reveal the origin of these structures and determine the corresponding critical momentum conditions by analyzing the values of [MATH], the dot product between the normalized prequench and postquench complex Bloch vectors. When Fisher zeros continuously cover the real-time axis, the density of Fisher zeros is further introduced to identify the critical times within these critical regions, at which the rate function becomes nonanalytic. We verify our results in a generalized non-Hermitian SSH model by quenching the Peierls phase and the non-Hermitian gain-loss strength, and also use the Jordan form to analyze the dynamics at postquench exceptional points, where the conventional Fisher zero formula is not applicable.
tldr: The paper analyzes anomalous structures of Fisher zero lines in biorthogonal dynamical quantum phase transitions for non-Hermitian quenches.
motivation: Fisher zeros of the Loschmidt amplitude can show unusual complex-time structures in non-Hermitian systems, and their origin and critical-momentum conditions are not fully understood.
method: The authors use a biorthogonal framework based on the dot product of normalized pre- and postquench complex Bloch vectors, introduce a Fisher-zero density for continuous real-time zero lines, and verify results in a generalized non-Hermitian SSH model, including postquench exceptional-point dynamics via the Jordan form.
result: They identify critical momentum conditions for divergence, separation, and axis-restricted Fisher-zero branches, and determine critical times where the rate function becomes nonanalytic when Fisher zeros cover the real-time axis.
conclusion: The biorthogonal approach explains anomalous Fisher-zero structures in non-Hermitian dynamical quantum phase transitions and extends the standard Fisher-zero formula to exceptional-point quenches.

title: Detailed Balance And Phase Transition In Nash Equilibria Of Mean-field Ising Game
authors: Ken Hiura, Hajime Koike, Kiyoshi Kanazawa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a finite-state mean-field game with entropic control cost. In the large population limit, we show that its stationary Nash equilibria satisfy the detailed balance condition and their distributions take the Gibbsian form with the value function playing the role of a Hamiltonian. We apply the entropic control cost to a ferromagnetic mean-field Ising game and investigate its stationary and non-stationary Nash equilibria. We find that the stationary Nash equilibria exhibit a second-order phase transition from disordered to ordered equilibria as temperature decreases. A center-manifold reduction yields non-stationary Nash equilibrium near the critical temperature and reveals the critical slowing down in the relaxation toward the stationary Nash equilibrium.
tldr: The paper studies stationary and non-stationary Nash equilibria in a finite-state mean-field Ising game with entropic control cost, showing Gibbsian equilibria, detailed balance, and a second-order phase transition.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how entropic control costs shape equilibrium structure and phase transitions in mean-field games, using the Ising game as a concrete ferromagnetic example.
method: They analyze a finite-state mean-field game in the large-population limit, prove detailed balance for stationary Nash equilibria, derive Gibbsian equilibrium distributions, and apply center-manifold reduction near the critical temperature.
result: Stationary Nash equilibria exhibit a second-order phase transition from disordered to ordered states as temperature decreases, and non-stationary equilibria near criticality show critical slowing down.
conclusion: The work connects mean-field game equilibria to Gibbsian statistical mechanics and characterizes critical dynamics, but it is a classical game-theory/statistical-physics result with no direct quantum information or quantum thermodynamics content.

title: Optically Gated Transduction Enables Silicon Electrical Readout Of Mid-infrared Light
authors: Shutao Zhang, Jiaqing Shen, Chongwu Wang, Jiahui Xu, Wei Chen, Qing Yang Steve Wu, Yan Liu, Xie Yuen Gok, Febiana Tjiptoharsono, Xiaogang Liu, Qi Jie Wang, Joel K. W. Yang, Jinfeng Zhu, Zhaogang Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon is the dominant platform for integrated photonics, yet its wide electronic bandgap of 1.1 eV fundamentally prevents efficient detection of mid-infrared (MIR) photons through direct valence band to conduction band excitation. Existing approaches therefore seek to enhance sub-bandgap absorption or introduce external infrared absorbers. Here we demonstrate a profoundly different detection strategy based on optically gated transduction, in which MIR photons modulate a pre-established excitation state rather than directly generating photocarriers. Our device integrates Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticles with an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface supporting dual resonances that simultaneously enhances optical gating in the near infrared and resonantly couples incident MIR radiation. The MIR illumination redistributes the Nd3+ emission pathways, producing an optical-state change that is converted into an electrical signal through a silicon Schottky junction. The device achieves room-temperature zero-bias detection at 6.8 um with a modulation responsivity of 103 uA/W and resolves combined gate and MIR inputs into three electrically distinguishable current states. Rather than extending silicon absorption into the infrared, this work establishes gated optical transduction as a route for reading MIR optical information on a silicon platform, opening opportunities for integrated infrared sensing, signal processing and programmable photonic systems.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a silicon-based mid-infrared detector that uses Nd3+-doped nanoparticle upconversion combined with an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface to convert MIR illumination into an electrically readable signal at room temperature and zero bias.
motivation: Silicon's 1.1 eV bandgap blocks direct MIR detection, and existing sub-bandgap absorption or external-absorber approaches are inefficient; a new transduction strategy is needed to read MIR light on a silicon photonics platform.
method: Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticles are integrated with a dual-resonance inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface, so that MIR light modulates a pre-established near-infrared optical excitation state rather than generating photocarriers directly; the optical-state change is transduced into current via a silicon Schottky junction.
result: The device achieves room-temperature, zero-bias detection at 6.8 um with a modulation responsivity of 103 uA/W and resolves combined gate and MIR inputs into three electrically distinguishable current states.
conclusion: Optically gated transduction offers a route to reading mid-infrared optical information on silicon, with potential for integrated infrared sensing, signal processing, and programmable photonic systems.

title: Constructive Cavity Method For Ising Restricted And Deep Boltzmann Machines With Gaussian Couplings
authors: Simone Franchini, Francesco Concetti, Giampiero Bardella, Liming Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) to the dense, Ising type, restricted and deep Boltzmann machine with Gaussian couplings between adjacent layers. After identifying the core and interface contributions, CCM identifies the blanket decomposition of the cavity variables with the Aizenman--Sims--Starr random overlap structure. We apply the Random Energy Model (REM) universality ansatz to represent the cavity free energies by those of a generalized random energy model (GREM) and evaluate them recursively through Poisson point processes (PPPs). In the layer-wise gauge each layer is cut with its own cumulative fraction [MATH], with [MATH], where [MATH]. Here [MATH] is the cumulative blanket union up to blanket [MATH]. The index [MATH] labels architectural layers, whereas [MATH] labels the blankets. The dependence on the multilayer geometry is carried by the two matrices [MATH] and [MATH]. The constructive cavity field in layer [MATH] has blanket variances [MATH], while the correction field has blanket variances [MATH]. The nested REM--PPP average gives the finite-level constructive cavity functional [MATH]. The balanced scalar gauge is recovered by imposing [MATH]. Selecting the physical value in the non-convex multilayer regime is a separate problem.
tldr: The paper develops a constructive cavity method for dense Ising restricted and deep Boltzmann machines with Gaussian couplings, using random-energy-model universality and Poisson point processes to compute cavity free energies.
motivation: The work aims to analyze dense multilayer Boltzmann machines by extending cavity-method techniques from disordered statistical mechanics to architectures with Gaussian interlayer couplings.
method: It decomposes cavity variables into core and interface contributions, maps the blanket structure to Aizenman-Sims-Starr random overlaps, and approximates cavity free energies via a generalized random energy model evaluated recursively with Poisson point processes.
result: The method yields a finite-level constructive cavity functional in a layer-wise gauge, with multilayer geometry encoded by two matrices controlling blanket variances and correction fields.
conclusion: The constructive cavity framework provides a statistical-physics approach to dense deep Boltzmann machines, though selecting the physical solution in the non-convex multilayer regime remains an open problem.

title: What Has Actually Been Proved? Auditable Paper-to-Lean Alignment With LeanTrail
authors: Fabricio Venturim, Leighton Estrada, Claudio Silva, Jorge Poco
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compiler feedback certifies that Lean accepts a declaration, not that the declaration captures the intended result: a repository can compile while a central theorem is weakened, merely auxiliary, or transitively dependent on sorry. Formalization progress should instead be measured against the source paper, in terms of its paper items: definitions, lemmas, and theorems. LeanTrail implements this view as a post-hoc, tool-agnostic audit: deterministic retrieval proposes candidate counterparts for each paper item in the Lean repository and, when available, the Blueprint; a language model judges statement-level correspondence, only among those candidates; and proof completeness comes from a deterministic transitive dependency audit never exposed to the model. Fusion assigns each item one of five coverage states, from Formalized to Missing, each backed by inspectable evidence. On consensus annotations of 98 items from three Lean projects, with three runs of each of two judge models, LeanTrail assigns the correct coverage state to 91.8% (Gemini 3.8 Flash) and 92.5% (GPT-6 Sol) of items. 96-97 of the 98 states are identical across runs, and GPT-6 Sol never reports a Partial item as Formalized. Uncovered items form a natural task queue for formalization agents, anchored to the specification rather than the compiler.
tldr: LeanTrail is a post-hoc, tool-agnostic auditing pipeline that checks whether Lean formalizations actually capture the definitions, lemmas, and theorems of the source paper, rather than merely compiling.
motivation: Compiler acceptance only certifies that a declaration type-checks, not that the formalized statement matches the intended paper result; theorems can be weakened, made auxiliary, or depend on sorry, so progress must be measured against the paper's items.
method: Deterministic retrieval proposes candidate Lean/Blueprint counterparts for each paper item, an LLM judge (restricted to those candidates) assesses statement-level correspondence, and a deterministic transitive dependency audit supplies proof completeness; fusion assigns one of five coverage states with inspectable evidence.
result: On consensus annotations of 98 items from three Lean projects with three runs of two judge models, LeanTrail reaches 91.8% (Gemini 3.8 Flash) and 92.5% (GPT-6 Sol) coverage-state accuracy, with 96-97 of 98 states stable across runs.
conclusion: LLM-assisted, evidence-backed auditing gives a reliable measure of paper-to-formalization alignment and yields a natural task queue of uncovered items for formalization agents.

title: Bayesian Inference In Partially Observed Critical Systems
authors: Mihika Singhania
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed before a global average can be inferred with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from [MATH] uniformly sampled cards, has relative uncertainty [MATH], independent of the deck size [MATH]. The law of total variance exposes a second error, the floor [MATH], which arises because the observed configuration is a single draw from equilibrium: no relative tolerance below [MATH] can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle we derive [MATH] and show that the posterior remains calibrated. At the critical point of the two-dimensional Ising model the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near [MATH]; its mean-field limit is [MATH]. For correlated fields read by sensor networks, the usual 95\% interval covers the ensemble mean in 7\% of cases. Bounding the floor from one realisation, as in single-chain Monte Carlo diagnostics, requires an assumption on the decay of correlations.
tldr: The paper studies Bayesian inference of global averages from partial observations in random and critical classical systems, identifying a variance floor set by equilibrium fluctuations.
motivation: It asks how much of a large random system must be observed to infer global averages with controlled uncertainty, and how single-realization sampling limits certifiable precision.
method: The author uses a conjugate Bayesian estimator for the random transposition shuffle and analyzes the law of total variance, then applies the framework to the 2D Ising model at criticality and to correlated sensor-network fields.
result: For the shuffle, the relative uncertainty scales inversely with the square root of the number of sampled cards and is independent of deck size, while a floor prevents certifying tolerances below a finite value; at the 2D Ising critical point the energy floor vanishes but the magnetization floor remains near a constant.
conclusion: Partial observation of critical or correlated systems faces intrinsic inference limits from equilibrium fluctuations, and bounding these limits from a single realization requires assumptions about correlation decay.

title: Cutting, Shuffling And Diffusion As A Coarsening Process
authors: Daniel Lester, Tanguy Leborgne, Joris Heyman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cutting and shuffling (CS) rearranges fluid without stretching, but homogenisation requires diffusion (D); this interaction is not well understood. We show that CSD is a coarsening process, with scale [MATH] rather than the Batchelor scale, and that cutting acts as a fractional Laplacian in wavenumber, giving the exact mixing rate [MATH] for [MATH] cuts per event at rate [MATH], with [MATH] the first zero of [MATH]. This holds in any dimension for random and deterministic protocols, extends to finite-time mixing, and places CSD in a known non-equilibrium universality class.
tldr: The paper shows that cutting-and-shuffling combined with diffusion (CSD) is a coarsening process whose mixing rate is set by a fractional-Laplacian action of cutting in wavenumber space.
motivation: Cutting and shuffling rearranges fluid without stretching, and homogenisation requires diffusion, but the interplay between the two mechanisms was poorly understood.
method: The authors treat cutting as a fractional Laplacian in wavenumber space and derive exact mixing rates for random and deterministic protocols with m cuts per event at a given rate, in arbitrary dimension, including finite-time behaviour.
result: The characteristic length scale follows a coarsening law rather than the Batchelor scale, and the exact mixing rate is expressed via the first zero of a Bessel-type function, valid across dimensions and protocols.
conclusion: CSD is placed within a known non-equilibrium universality class, giving a unified framework for cutting, shuffling and diffusion in mixing flows.

title: Evaluation Of Upper-scale Mechanical Parameters Of Particulate Aluminum-based Nanocomposites From Molecular Simulations
authors: Bartosz Bucholc, Marcin Ma\'zdziarz, Szymon Nosewicz
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper focuses on the numerical and analytical determination of the mechanical parameters of aluminum-matrix nanocomposites using atomistic-scale simulations within a multiscale modeling framework. Molecular statics simulations were employed to evaluate the tensile and compressive behavior of Al based composites reinforced with nanosized alumina particles. Two classes of atomistic models were investigated. First, a unit-cell model containing a single Al2O3 monocrystal embedded in an aluminum matrix was used to examine the influence of the volume fraction of the ceramic inclusion on the effective mechanical properties. Second, a polycrystalline RVE model comprising an alumina particle was analyzed to assess the effect of the number of Al grains on effective properties. For each case, the mechanical response was characterized by stress-strain curves, enabling the identification of upper-scale material parameters associated with the elastic regime (bulk, shear and Young's modulus) and the damage stage (ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain). The isotropized elastic constants evaluated from molecular simulations were compared with classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds to assess their applicability in the elastic regime. Finally, atomistic-scale simulation outputs provided insight into the dominant deformation/damage mechanisms (brittle versus ductile) and fracture modes (transgranular versus intergranular).
tldr: Molecular statics simulations are used to extract effective mechanical parameters of alumina-reinforced aluminum nanocomposites for multiscale modeling.
motivation: Upper-scale continuum models of metal-matrix nanocomposites require reliable elastic and damage parameters that are difficult to obtain experimentally at the nanoscale.
method: Unit-cell and polycrystalline representative volume element atomistic models of Al2O3 inclusions in an Al matrix were simulated under tension and compression, yielding stress-strain curves and isotropized elastic constants compared with Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds.
result: Bulk, shear and Young's moduli plus ultimate strength, ultimate strain and failure strain were identified as functions of inclusion volume fraction and grain count, with dominant brittle/ductile and transgranular/intergranular failure modes characterized.
conclusion: Atomistic simulation provides a practical route to calibrate upper-scale material parameters for particulate aluminum nanocomposites, with classical bounds holding reasonably in the elastic regime.

title: Phase Transitions In Mismatched Bayesian Inference For The Ising Model
authors: Xinyu Sun, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, Hong Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian inference with a mismatched model can develop an overconfident phase, characterized by posterior agreement without faithful reconstruction of the true state. We study Bayesian inference from noisy bond measurements of an Ising model in its paramagnetic phase, with true inverse temperature [MATH] and measurement-noise strength [MATH], while inference assumes corresponding parameters [MATH] and [MATH]. Using replica field theory, we analytically show that the overconfidence phase can occur when inference underestimates the measurement noise ([MATH]) or assumes a lower prior temperature than the true one ([MATH]). An exact change of variables maps the problem to a correlated random-bond Ising model, where the informative, uninformative, and overconfident phases correspond to ferromagnetic, paramagnetic, and spin-glass phases, respectively. We further perform Monte Carlo simulations of the mapped model in three dimensions and establish a finite overconfident region between the informative and uninformative phases, consistent with our analytical prediction. Finally, we show that the true model parameters can be inferred directly from the measurement records, providing a natural route to calibrating the inference model.
tldr: The paper analyzes phase transitions in mismatched Bayesian inference for noisy Ising-model measurements, mapping overconfidence to a spin-glass phase in a correlated random-bond Ising model.
motivation: Bayesian inference with an incorrect model can become overconfident, producing posterior agreement without faithful reconstruction of the true state; the authors aim to characterize when this occurs.
method: They use replica field theory to derive phase boundaries analytically and map the inference problem to a correlated random-bond Ising model, then perform Monte Carlo simulations in three dimensions.
result: Overconfidence arises when the inferred measurement noise is underestimated or the inferred prior temperature is lower than the true one, and simulations confirm a finite overconfident region between informative and uninformative phases.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical-mechanics understanding of mismatched Bayesian inference and suggests that true model parameters can be inferred directly from measurement records for calibration.

title: Subpercent Accuracy In Molecular Electric Quadrupole Coupling: Nuclear-size And Relativistic Effects In RaF
authors: Leonid V. Skripnikov, Michail Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, Carlos M. Fajardo-Zambrano
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the [MATH] electronic ground state is [MATH] a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.
tldr: Benchmark relativistic coupled-cluster calculations of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in RaF, including finite-nuclear-size effects, achieve subpercent accuracy for the effective electric field gradient.
motivation: Accurate knowledge of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling in RaF is needed to extract nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision from future measurements.
method: The authors use the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian with coupled-cluster theory up to perturbative quadruple excitations, and they compare Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models to assess finite-nuclear-size and penetration corrections.
result: They recommend an effective electric field gradient for the RaF ground state with an uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude relative to previous studies, finding that the EFG is nearly insensitive to the monopole nuclear charge shape at fixed rms radius.
conclusion: The results provide a high-accuracy reference for future RaF hyperfine measurements and for determining Ra nuclear quadrupole moments, but the work is specialized molecular quantum chemistry and does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Radial Power-like Potentials: From The Bohr-Sommerfeld $\ell \neq 0$ State Energies To The Exact Ones
authors: A. V. Turbiner J. C. Del Valle
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two new Bohr-Sommerfeld (B-S) type quantization conditions for [MATH]-dimensional radial potentials are proposed for non-singular and singular potentials, respectively. The power-like potentials for [MATH] and [MATH] (that corresponds to [MATH]) are studied in detail for radial quantum numbers [MATH] and for angular momenta [MATH] in dimensions [MATH]. It is shown that for large [MATH] the B-S energies [MATH] always tend to the exact ones. For [MATH] (the radial harmonic oscillator) and [MATH] (the [MATH]-dimensional analogue of the [MATH] Coulomb potential) the B-S spectrum coincides with the exact one for the first and second quantization conditions, respectively. In general, up to a small parametric shift of the radial quantum number, the analytic formulas for the energy spectrum can be written for arbitrary power-like potential. A comparison of [MATH] with the energies [MATH], obtained for the radial potentials modified by the Langer correction for [MATH], are in good agreement in general: in detail, it was checked for the quartic oscillator [MATH]. It is demonstrated that introducing a dimensionless {\it WKB correction} [MATH] into the r.h.s. of the proposed B-S type quantization condition allows us to reproduce the exact energies with [MATH] being very small for positive degrees [MATH] and sufficiently small for non-positive ones [MATH] for all [MATH] studied.
tldr: The authors propose two new Bohr-Sommerfeld-type quantization conditions for D-dimensional radial power-like potentials and show that the resulting spectra approach the exact energies for large radial quantum numbers.
motivation: Standard semiclassical quantization of radial potentials suffers from Langer-type corrections and fails to reproduce exact spectra for low-lying states; a more accurate quantization condition is therefore desirable.
method: Two modified Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions (for singular and non-singular potentials) are derived and tested numerically for power-law potentials V(r) ~ r^nu with nu = 2, 4, -1, 0, and a dimensionless WKB correction term is introduced to improve accuracy.
result: The B-S spectra converge to the exact energies as the radial quantum number grows, become exact for the harmonic oscillator and Coulomb cases, and reproduce exact energies to high precision once a small WKB correction is included.
conclusion: The proposed quantization conditions provide accurate analytic energy formulas for arbitrary power-like radial potentials, generalizing and improving upon the Langer-corrected WKB approach.

title: Dynamical Behaviour Of The Mass Tensor In The Lattice
authors: Josu\'e Calle, Diego Sanjin\'es, Evaristo Mamani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study with the semiclassical model the dynamics of a particle moving in a orthorrombic lattice by the hopping mechanism in the presence of a static Coulomb field and a rapidly oscillating homogeneous field. Based on results for the anisotropic Kepler problem, where a chaotic trajectory arises due to different masses of the particle in the X and Y directions, and since this result is also obtained in the rectangular lattice at the continuum limit, the application of the oscillating field allows reparameterizing the effective masses so that they become equal in both directions. Thus, the result is an elliptic trajectory in the continuum limit of the lattice. This chaos-order transition is confirmed by the calculation of Lyapunov exponents for the different trajectories. It is also found that the application of an external magnetic field in the Z direction of the lattice yields chaos control which can be generalized beyond the simple case of the circular trajectory shown in this work. The previous scheme of chaos control was extended for trajectories in 3D in the continuum limit of the orthorrombic lattice which is also equivalent to the far region approximation where the particle moves with respect to the Coulomb field origin. In this case it found that the chaos control technique permits to observe two different dynamical regimes which, although consistent with Bohr-van Leeuwen theorem, suggests that an observable way to distinguish one from the other is to be sought.
tldr: The paper studies semiclassical particle dynamics in an orthorhombic lattice, showing that oscillating and magnetic fields can reparameterize effective masses and control chaos.
motivation: Anisotropic effective masses in lattices can induce chaotic trajectories; the authors aim to control this chaos via external driving and magnetic fields.
method: A semiclassical hopping model is used with a static Coulomb field and a rapidly oscillating homogeneous field, supported by Lyapunov exponent calculations and extensions to 3D continuum limits.
result: The oscillating field equalizes effective masses along different directions, producing elliptic trajectories, while a magnetic field provides chaos control and reveals two dynamical regimes.
conclusion: External fields can tune mass anisotropy and transitions between chaotic and ordered dynamics in lattice systems, with possible extensions beyond circular trajectories.

title: Feedback Autocratic Strategies In Stochastic Games
authors: Masahiko Ueda
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A stochastic game is an optimal control problem for multiple agents in a stochastic environment. Stochastic games contain important practical problems, related to environmental issues or traffic flows. If the number of environmental states is one, such stochastic games are called repeated games. In repeated games, several strategies which unilaterally control payoffs have been proposed, and these strategies work in a mechanism similar to feedback control. In this paper, we generalize these strategies as feedback strategies in stochastic games, and investigate their properties. In particular, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for such feedback strategies to work as controllers of payoffs under some assumptions. We demonstrate the performance of such feedback strategies in several examples related to social dilemmas. Our findings connect the theory of payoff control in repeated games to the theory of feedback control in stochastic games.
tldr: The paper generalizes payoff-controlling autocratic strategies from repeated games to stochastic games and characterizes when feedback strategies can unilaterally control payoffs.
motivation: Repeated games contain strategies that unilaterally control payoffs through feedback-like mechanisms, and the author aims to extend this payoff-control framework to stochastic games with multiple environmental states.
method: The author defines feedback autocratic strategies for stochastic games and derives a necessary and sufficient condition under stated assumptions for these strategies to act as payoff controllers, supported by examples from social dilemmas.
result: A necessary and sufficient condition is provided for feedback strategies to control payoffs in stochastic games, and examples illustrate their performance in social-dilemma settings.
conclusion: The work connects payoff control theory in repeated games with feedback control theory in stochastic games, but it does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Observable Diameter Of Product Measures With A Power-type Interior Zero
authors: Takashi Shioya
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the asymptotic order of the observable diameter of [MATH]-product spaces associated with a probability measure on [MATH] whose density has a power-type interior zero. Different vanishing orders are allowed on the two sides of the zero. For every [MATH], we obtain sharp two-sided estimates and show that the asymptotic order is governed by the larger of the two vanishing orders. In the case [MATH], the transition occurs exactly at the threshold for the spectral gap.
tldr: A purely geometric/measure-theoretic paper determining the asymptotic order of the observable diameter of product spaces whose measure density has a power-type interior zero.
motivation: Observable diameter, a measure-concentration concept introduced by Gromov, quantifies the spread of Lipschitz functions under a measure; the author aims to characterize it for product measures with singular (vanishing) densities.
method: Sharp two-sided estimates are derived for the observable diameter of product spaces, allowing different vanishing orders on the two sides of the interior zero of the density, and compared against the spectral gap threshold in the special case of interest.
result: The asymptotic order is shown to be governed by the larger of the two vanishing orders, with sharp estimates valid for every parameter value, and a transition occurring exactly at the spectral-gap threshold in the special case.
conclusion: The paper fully characterizes concentration behavior for this class of product measures, linking observable diameter asymptotics to the vanishing orders of the density and to spectral-gap phenomena.

title: On The Fundamental Limits Of Bistatic Isac Over Vector Channels
authors: Dongsheng Peng, Lei Yu, Ping Chen, Jun Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the fundamental limits of bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems over vector channels. We first consider a class of parallel channels in which, on each component channel, the channel from the transmitter (Tx) to the communication receiver (Rx) is degraded with respect to the channel from the Tx to the sensing Rx, or vice versa, where the direction of degradation may vary across component channels. For this class of channels, we establish matching achievability and converse results, which yield a single-letter characterization of the capacity-distortion function [MATH]. For parallel Gaussian channels with additive Gaussian states, the evaluation of the capacity-distortion-power function [MATH] under the squared error distortion measure reduces to a joint power and distortion allocation problem across the component channels. We then extend the analysis to general vector channels and derive single-letter lower and upper bounds on [MATH]. In particular, for vector Gaussian channels with additive Gaussian states, we prove the optimality of Gaussian superposition coding without requiring a global degradation order between the communication and sensing channels, by combining the channel enhancement technique with a matrix extremal inequality based on Fisher information. This leads to an exact characterization of [MATH].
tldr: The paper characterizes fundamental capacity-distortion limits for bistatic integrated sensing and communication over parallel and vector Gaussian channels.
motivation: ISAC systems require a unified information-theoretic understanding of the tradeoff between communication rate and sensing distortion, especially when the communication and sensing channels are not globally ordered.
method: The authors derive matching achievability and converse bounds for parallel degraded channels, reduce Gaussian evaluation to joint power and distortion allocation, and extend to vector channels using channel enhancement and a Fisher-information-based matrix extremal inequality.
result: They obtain single-letter capacity-distortion characterizations for parallel channels and exact capacity-distortion-power results for vector Gaussian channels under Gaussian superposition coding, without requiring a global degradation order.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental limits for classical bistatic ISAC over vector channels, but it does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Bayesian Replicator Dynamics And The Inversion Of Strict Dominance In Bimatrix Games
authors: Jaime Ruiz-Serra, Nihat Ay, Michael Harr\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Replicator dynamics, the central model of evolutionary game theory, describe populations evolving under selection and agents learning by trial and error. They also admit a third use: continuous-time Bayesian inference, in which an agent planning against an opponent accumulates evidence for each candidate strategy. Here we show that this use divides all two-player games into two classes. With the standard expected-utility payoff, the dynamics can be expressed as Bayesian updating only in games (with any number of actions) where no player has a dominant strategy. The logarithmic payoff of Ay and Erb admits the Bayesian representation in every game. Coordination, anti-coordination, and cyclic games share qualitative dynamics under both payoff definitions, with equilibria displaced and selection thresholds shifted. In contrast, the flows of every game with a dominant strategy are reversed between the payoff definitions, with the strictly dominant strategy eliminated under logarithmic payoffs. Cooperation therefore emerges in the Prisoner's Dilemma, and games of common interest converge to mutual defection. For two-action games the classification is complete and rests on an exact Hamiltonian structure shared by both payoff definitions. The structure gives a behavioural test: cycles in the classic Matching Pennies game have amplitude-independent period (isochronous) under logarithmic payoffs, but not under expected utility. Logarithmic evidence integration thus determines which strategic outcomes dynamical selection can reach, wherever learning approximates Bayesian updating.
tldr: The paper shows that Bayesian replicator dynamics with expected-utility versus logarithmic payoffs divides two-player games into distinct dynamical classes, reversing flows in games with dominant strategies and yielding testable behavioral signatures.
motivation: Replicator dynamics are usually studied as evolutionary or learning processes, but they can also be interpreted as continuous-time Bayesian inference; the authors ask when this Bayesian interpretation is valid and what consequences it has for game dynamics.
method: The authors compare replicator dynamics under standard expected-utility payoffs and logarithmic payoffs, derive conditions for a Bayesian updating representation, and analyze the resulting flows for bimatrix games including coordination, anti-coordination, cyclic, and dominant-strategy games.
result: Expected-utility dynamics admit a Bayesian representation only when no player has a dominant strategy, whereas logarithmic payoffs admit it for every game; in dominant-strategy games the flows are reversed, eliminating strictly dominant strategies under logarithmic payoffs, and two-action games have an exact Hamiltonian structure with isochronous cycles in Matching Pennies under logarithmic payoffs.
conclusion: Logarithmic evidence integration qualitatively changes which strategic outcomes dynamical selection can reach, providing a behavioral test that distinguishes Bayesian replicator dynamics from standard expected-utility selection.

title: Rethinking Channel Estimation For Fluid Antenna Systems: A Physics-Informed Operator Learning
authors: Zixin Wang, Lizhong Zheng, Yuanming Shi, Kaibin Huang, Khaled B. Letaief
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) leverage continuous reconfigurable apertures to transcend the spatial limits of fixed-position arrays, yet acquiring full-aperture channel state information (CSI) from sparse observations remains a formidable bottleneck. In this paper, we establish a continuous-field formulation for FAS by recasting channel estimation as a stochastic inverse field-reconstruction problem constrained by the projected Helmholtz model. Through electromagnetic information theory (EIT)-based spectral leakage analysis, we demonstrate that finite-aperture reconstruction induces an intrinsic convolutional relationship in the spectral domain, rendering the estimation task a fundamental frequency-domain inverse deconvolution problem. To solve this, we propose a U-shaped Fourier neural operator (UFNO) specifically tailored for noisy, underdetermined wireless environments. Furthermore, we leverage the Landau--Pollak theorem to derive an aperture-dependent EDoF bound that guides the spatial mode budget, and employ a physics-aware Sobolev loss to promote consistency in both channel values and spatial variations. Unlike conventional learning-based approaches, a single frozen UFNO can be directly evaluated at unseen spatial--frequency resolutions without resolution-specific retraining or explicit output interpolation. Extensive simulations show that our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks in accuracy while achieving orders-of-magnitude lower inference latency than iterative solvers at high spatial--frequency resolutions.
tldr: The paper formulates fluid antenna system channel estimation as a physics-informed inverse field-reconstruction problem and solves it with a U-shaped Fourier neural operator.
motivation: Fluid antenna systems require full-aperture CSI from sparse observations, which is a major bottleneck for continuous reconfigurable apertures.
method: The authors recast channel estimation as a stochastic inverse problem constrained by the projected Helmholtz model, analyze spectral leakage via electromagnetic information theory, and propose a U-shaped Fourier neural operator with a physics-aware Sobolev loss.
result: The proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks in accuracy and achieves orders-of-magnitude lower inference latency than iterative solvers at high spatial-frequency resolutions.
conclusion: Physics-informed operator learning provides an efficient resolution-agnostic approach to channel estimation in fluid antenna systems.

title: Quantifying And Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors
authors: Indraveni Chebolu, Seema Panghal, Arnab Mallick, Ch A S Murty
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security pipelines often fuse several data sources and protect a downstream model with a cross-source anomaly detector. Such detectors are usually judged by their clean false-positive rate and by how well they catch random corruption. Neither metric captures an adversary who controls some sources and targets a specific downstream decision. We propose a threat-quantification score, the , defined as the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm to the downstream task. The margin has a closed form, takes about [MATH]s per certificate, yields a minimum-evidence attack, and identifies task-relevant directions the detector cannot see. On a 17-channel industrial telemetry benchmark, a detector that flags 82.8\% of random single-channel corruptions is first-order blind on 64.7\% of task/subset pairs in an audit of one- to four-channel subsets. Task-conditioned manipulations cause more than twice as many falsely reassuring errors as generic stealthy ones, and more of them evade the alarm on four of five splits, mainly at small budgets. Used to prioritize audits on held-out subsets, the margin finds a median of four verified failures in ten checks, compared with none for random order and two for alarm-based ranking, and performs comparably to the task-gradient baseline. It also ranks vulnerable configurations of the learned GDN and TranAD detectors and of a five-source crop-yield panel.
tldr: The paper proposes a threat-quantification metric for stealthy source-manipulation attacks against multi-source anomaly detectors and uses it to prioritize audits.
motivation: Cross-source anomaly detectors are typically evaluated by false-positive rates and robustness to random corruption, which do not capture targeted adversaries controlling some data sources.
method: The authors define a margin score measuring the least detector evidence per unit downstream harm, derive a closed-form certificate, construct minimum-evidence attacks, and test on industrial telemetry and other benchmarks.
result: The metric exposes blind spots in detectors, shows task-conditioned manipulations evade alarms more often, and improves audit prioritization over random and alarm-based ranking.
conclusion: The proposed threat-quantification approach helps identify and prioritize stealthy source-manipulation vulnerabilities in multi-source anomaly-detection pipelines.

title: Complete Expanding Interval Maps Are Mixing
authors: E. L. O'neil, F. M. Tangerman, J. J. P. Veerman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new and elementary proof that certain smooth, complete, expanding maps from the interval to itself are mixing.
tldr: The paper provides a new, elementary proof that smooth, complete, expanding maps of the interval are mixing.
motivation: Mixing is a fundamental ergodic property of dynamical systems, and existing proofs for expanding interval maps are considered unnecessarily heavy or indirect; the authors seek a simpler, self-contained argument.
method: A purely analytic/ergodic-theoretic approach: exploiting expansion and completeness of the smooth interval map to control the decay of correlations between measurable sets under iterates.
result: An elementary proof establishing that smooth complete expanding interval maps exhibit the mixing property.
conclusion: The result simplifies and clarifies a known theorem in one-dimensional dynamics, but remains within pure ergodic theory and has no bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum hardware.

title: A Fast Algorithm For Quaternion Tensor Singular Value Decomposition Under The QT-Product With Applications To Color Video Processing
authors: Daochang Zhang, Yue Zhao, Jingqian Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the complex representation of quaternion matrices, this paper revisits the quaternion tensor singular value decomposition (QT-SVD) under the QT-product and establishes the corresponding [MATH]-block circulant matrix decomposition. We develop an efficient implementation of the QT-SVD. Numerical experiments show that this implementation is substantially faster than QT-SVD based on the quaternion matrix SVD approach \cite[Theorem~2.3]{AMLzhang2022} while maintaining high numerical accuracy. We further apply the QT-SVD to color video encryption and reconstruction. Experiments on five DAVIS video sequences show that the QT-SVD achieves higher reconstruction quality and shorter decomposition times than the quaternion T-SVD under the same processing procedure. Both methods exhibit comparable ciphertext statistics and differential sensitivity, while the QT-SVD introduces less additional distortion under the tested input perturbations.
tldr: The paper develops a faster implementation of quaternion tensor singular value decomposition under the QT-product and applies it to color video encryption and reconstruction.
motivation: Quaternion-based tensor decompositions can handle color video data holistically by encoding RGB channels in quaternion units, but existing QT-SVD implementations based on quaternion matrix SVD are computationally slow.
method: Using the complex representation of quaternion matrices, the authors revisit QT-SVD under the QT-product, derive a corresponding block-circulant matrix decomposition, and build an efficient algorithmic implementation.
result: The implementation is substantially faster than the quaternion-matrix-SVD-based approach while retaining high numerical accuracy, and on five DAVIS video sequences it yields better reconstruction quality and shorter decomposition times than quaternion T-SVD, with comparable encryption statistics and less distortion under input perturbations.
conclusion: The proposed fast QT-SVD is an efficient tool for color video encryption and reconstruction, offering speed and quality advantages over prior quaternion tensor decompositions.

title: Wasserstein Approximation Of Measures Via Orthogonal Frames: Statistical And Computational Complexities
authors: Mateo D\'iaz, Nicol\'as Garc\'ia Trillos, Daniel L\'opez-Casta\~no, Congwei Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dimension-reduction methods such as PCA identify a subspace capturing most of the variation in the data, but not a distinguished basis within it. Selecting a basis in which the samples are sparsely represented is a recurring task in unsupervised learning, addressed by methods in factor analysis, dictionary learning, and subspace clustering. We pose this task as Wasserstein approximation of the data distribution by measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame, which, in turn, reduces to a nonsmooth optimization problem over the orthogonal group [MATH]. We show that, under mild assumptions, both empirical risk minimizers and a locally initialized stochastic gradient method recover the population-optimal frame at the near-parametric rate [MATH], where [MATH] is the sample size. The main difficulty is that, although the population objective is smooth, the empirical objective is not-this mismatch precludes standard covering arguments.
