We overcome this issue by replacing Lipschitz continuity of the empirical gradient with a coarsely Lipschitz bound, a tool that may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments support our theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper recasts sparse basis selection for dimension-reduced data as a Wasserstein approximation of the empirical distribution by measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame, and analyzes statistical and computational complexity of the resulting nonsmooth optimization over the orthogonal group.
motivation: Methods like PCA find a low-dimensional subspace but not a distinguished sparse basis, a gap addressed piecemeal by factor analysis, dictionary learning, and subspace clustering; the authors seek a principled distribution-matching formulation with provable guarantees.
method: The task is posed as minimizing a Wasserstein distance between the data distribution and measures supported on frame axes, yielding a nonsmooth optimization over the orthogonal group; the analysis handles the smooth-population/nonsmooth-empirical mismatch by replacing Lipschitz continuity of the empirical gradient with a coarsely Lipschitz bound, and studies a locally initialized stochastic gradient method.
result: Under mild assumptions, both empirical risk minimizers and the locally initialized stochastic gradient descent recover the population-optimal frame at a near-parametric rate in the sample size, with numerical experiments supporting the theory.
conclusion: The work provides statistical and computational guarantees for orthogonal-frame-based sparse representation via optimal transport, and introduces a coarsely Lipschitz tool of potentially independent interest.

title: Merkle-Tree-Based Verifiable Public Data Auditing For Cloud Object Storage Using Smart Contracts
authors: Siri Reddy Tadi, K. Gangadhara Rao, M. Venu Gopalachari, C. Chetann Reddy, Jaswanth Bhimireddy
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Owners of data in cloud object storage cannot directly check whether the provider still keeps every object unchanged. Existing research mostly checks blocks inside files or relies on third-party auditors, and less attention has been given to checking each object against a public blockchain reference while measuring the cost. A full-data audit downloads every object and compares it with a saved hash list, which is slow and only as reliable as that list. We propose a public auditing system in which the SHA-256 hash of each object and its name forms a leaf of a Merkle tree, so the whole dataset is represented by one Merkle root. This root is stored in an Ethereum smart contract as a trusted public record, while the objects stay with the provider. An auditor downloads an object, rebuilds the root using a short Merkle proof and compares it with the stored root, marking the object as intact, modified or missing. In five experiments on an S3-compatible store and a local Hardhat blockchain (normal audit, single- and multiple-object tampering, deletion and scalability), the system detected 15 of 15 single modifications, 2,205 of 2,205 modified objects and 830 of 830 deleted objects with no false alarms. The proof needed only 14 hashes for 10,000 objects, so checking one object took about 10 ms and a 100-object sample about 150 ms regardless of dataset size, while a full audit of 10,000 objects (14.3 s) took about as long as downloading them (13.5 s). Storing the root cost 91,863 gas, 252 times less than storing 1,000 hashes on-chain. The system thus shows exactly which objects were modified or are missing, with its main savings coming from checking selected objects.
tldr: A Merkle-tree and Ethereum smart-contract based public auditing scheme for verifying integrity of objects in cloud object storage.
motivation: Cloud storage owners cannot directly verify that providers retain every object unmodified, and existing block-level or third-party-auditor approaches are slow or only as trustworthy as a saved hash list.
method: Each object's SHA-256 hash together with its name forms a Merkle tree leaf; the root is stored in an Ethereum smart contract, and auditors verify individual objects by downloading them, reconstructing the root from a short Merkle proof, and comparing against the on-chain root.
result: Experiments on an S3-compatible store and local Hardhat blockchain detected all 15 single modifications, 2,205/2,205 modified objects, and 830/830 deletions with no false alarms, using 14 hashes for 10,000 objects (~10 ms per object), with root storage costing 91,863 gas.
conclusion: The system precisely identifies modified or missing objects and achieves its main efficiency gains by auditing selected objects rather than full datasets.

title: Learning-Augmented Coordination Mechanisms
authors: George Christodoulou, Vasilis Christoforidis, Alkmini Sgouritsa, Ioannis Vlachos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inefficiency of decentralized resource allocation is classically measured by the Price of Anarchy (PoA) and the Price of Stability (PoS). The most widely studied and foundational class of these models are atomic and non-atomic congestion games, for which a robust theory quantifying the inefficiency of equilibria is well-established. To mitigate the effects of selfish behavior, we employ Coordination Mechanisms, which modify resource costs to incentivize socially improved equilibria. However, standard Coordination Mechanisms assume unknown, adversarial demand, restricting positive results mainly to specialized networks such as parallel links. We address this limitation by studying learning-augmented coordination mechanisms, where the mechanism is endowed with a potentially inaccurate prediction of the demand. We study general atomic and non-atomic congestion games with polynomial latency functions of degree [MATH]. Our main positive result is a learning-augmented coordination mechanism tuned by a confidence parameter [MATH] which achieves a "best of both worlds" type of result: approximately optimal performance for an accurate prediction without sacrificing the worst-case guarantee of a good equilibrium (PoS). We further establish bounds on PoA-Robustness (worst equilibrium performance under cost modification). Our construction relies on transforming approximate equilibria of the original game into exact equilibria of the modified game using an approximate potential function. We complement our positive results with impossibility results. We first show that requiring all equilibria to have optimal social cost under an accurate prediction precludes bounded robustness. We also show a strong error tolerance limit in non-atomic games: even infinitesimal prediction errors can cause the performance of a mechanism with optimal consistency to revert to the original PoA.
tldr: The paper introduces learning-augmented coordination mechanisms that use a possibly inaccurate demand prediction to improve equilibrium efficiency in atomic and non-atomic congestion games with polynomial latency functions.
motivation: Classical coordination mechanisms assume adversarial unknown demand, which restricts positive results to special network topologies such as parallel links; accurate demand predictions could enable much better performance.
method: The authors design a confidence-parameterized coordination mechanism that modifies resource costs, and analyze it by transforming approximate equilibria of the original game into exact equilibria of the modified game via an approximate potential function, complemented by impossibility results.
result: The mechanism achieves a best-of-both-worlds guarantee: near-optimal social cost under accurate predictions while retaining the worst-case Price of Stability bound, along with bounds on Price-of-Anarchy robustness; impossibility results show that requiring optimality at all equilibria precludes bounded robustness, and that infinitesimal prediction errors in non-atomic games can degrade performance back to the original Price of Anarchy.
conclusion: Learning-augmented coordination mechanisms can substantially mitigate selfish inefficiency in general congestion games, but fundamental consistency-robustness tradeoffs and fragility to prediction error limit what is achievable.

title: Design Of DoF-Robust Mimo Via Generalized Pinching Antennas
authors: Zhiguo Ding, Robert Schober, H. Vincent Poor
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) are fundamental to the performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. However, the use of conventional fixed-location antennas introduces disparities in the users' distances to a common base station, which makes the multi-user channel matrix more susceptible to rank deficiency and, consequently, a loss of spatial DoF. This paper shows that generalized pinching antennas can be used to design a new form of MIMO robust to the loss of spatial DoF. In particular, by deploying pinching antennas in close proximity to the users, the resulting multi-user channel Gram matrix can have a well-conditioned, almost diagonal structure, which reduces its sensitivity to the users' spatial deployment as well as the risk of rank deficiency. Two performance metrics, namely the rank-deficiency probability and the outage probability, are used to evaluate the performance of pinching-antenna-assisted MIMO transmission. The presented analytical and simulation results demonstrate the capability of pinching antennas to preserve spatial DoF and provide ubiquitous connectivity by effectively supporting users at spatially separated locations.
tldr: The paper proposes a MIMO design using generalized pinching antennas placed near users to preserve spatial degrees of freedom and avoid rank deficiency in multi-user channels.
motivation: Conventional fixed-location antennas create distance disparities across users, making the multi-user channel matrix prone to rank deficiency and loss of spatial degrees of freedom.
method: Pinching antennas are deployed in close proximity to users so that the resulting multi-user channel Gram matrix becomes well-conditioned and nearly diagonal; rank-deficiency probability and outage probability are derived analytically and via simulation.
result: Analytical and simulation results show that pinching-antenna-assisted MIMO preserves spatial DoF and supports users at spatially separated locations, providing ubiquitous connectivity.
conclusion: Generalized pinching antennas offer a robust MIMO architecture against spatial DoF loss, improving reliability of multi-user downlink transmission.

title: Equivalence Between Rationality And Modular Invariance Under $C_2$-cofiniteness
authors: Hao Wang (school Of Mathematics, Northwest University, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China), Jiang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for a simple and [MATH]-cofinite vertex operator algebra, the rationality is equivalent to the modular invariance of the space of complete ordinary one-point trace functions of its irreducible modules. This proves a conjecture given by Dong-Ren in , which is also the inverse theorem of Zhu's modular invariance theorem .
tldr: The paper proves that for simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebras, rationality is equivalent to modular invariance of the space of complete ordinary one-point trace functions of irreducible modules.
motivation: This addresses a conjecture of Dong-Ren and provides an inverse to Zhu's modular invariance theorem in the setting of vertex operator algebras.
method: The authors work within the mathematical theory of vertex operator algebras, using C2-cofiniteness and modular invariance properties of trace functions on irreducible modules.
result: They establish an equivalence between rationality and modular invariance of the relevant space of one-point trace functions for simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebras.
conclusion: The result confirms the Dong-Ren conjecture and completes the inverse direction of Zhu's modular invariance theorem under C2-cofiniteness assumptions.

title: Stability Analysis Of The Lane--Emden Equation Of Index $n=5$ Describing Polytropic Gas Spheres
authors: Ronald Adams S. C. Mancas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Lane--Emden equation of index [MATH], the critical polytropic case separating finite-radius from infinite-radius self-gravitating equilibria. The scaling family [MATH] generates a neutral mode [MATH] about the Schuster profile. Schuster's transformation and a logarithmic variable reduce the equation to the autonomous Hamiltonian system [MATH] with a first integral. Besides the Schuster (separatrix) and Srivastava solutions, every orbit crossing [MATH] is given in closed form by a Weierstrass [MATH]-function, and the closed forms agree with direct numerical integration to about [MATH]. Up to scaling and sign, the Schuster solution is the only solution regular at the center, and it separates positive solutions from solutions with infinitely many zeros. In homology-invariant variables the singular solution [MATH] is a center exactly at [MATH], where its stability changes. For a distance-varying Emden--Fowler system with a shifted equilibrium we prove that at [MATH] the unique equilibrium is linearly and nonlinearly unstable. Finally, the linearization about the Schuster profile is the Schr\"odinger operator [MATH] on [MATH]. Its Friedrichs extension has essential spectrum [MATH], a threshold resonance at [MATH] carried by the non-normalizable scaling mode, and exactly one negative eigenvalue, [MATH], so the Schuster profile is a saddle point of the associated energy functional.
tldr: A mathematical stability analysis of the Lane–Emden equation of index n=5, characterizing its solutions via an autonomous Hamiltonian reduction and a Schrödinger-operator linearization.
motivation: The critical index n=5 separates finite-radius from infinite-radius polytropic self-gravitating equilibria, making its stability properties mathematically important for models of polytropic gas spheres.
method: Schuster's transformation and a logarithmic variable reduce the equation to an autonomous Hamiltonian system with a first integral; solutions are expressed in closed form via Weierstrass elliptic functions, and stability is analyzed via homology-invariant variables and the Friedrichs extension of the linearized Schrödinger operator.
result: The Schuster solution is the unique center-regular solution, separating positive solutions from oscillatory ones; the singular solution is a center exactly at n=5, the shifted-equilibrium Emden–Fowler system is unstable there, and the linearized operator has essential spectrum [0,∞), a threshold resonance from the scaling mode, and exactly one negative eigenvalue.
conclusion: The Schuster profile is a saddle point of the associated energy functional, and the stability transition at n=5 is fully characterized in closed form.

title: Derivation Of Oh Sum Rules Without Rayleigh--Jeans Approximation: A Powerful Tool For Measuring The Variation Of Fundamental Physical Constants
authors: Minfeng Gu Renzhi Su
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that the optical depths of any OH [MATH]-doublet quartet obey one exact linear relation in every velocity channel. No approximation is needed. The only exception is the [MATH] [MATH] level, which has three transitions only, because its [MATH] line is strictly forbidden. The relation is [MATH], where [MATH], [MATH], and the [MATH] are reduced transition dipole moments derived from the catalogued Einstein [MATH] coefficients. It holds equally for gas in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), for non-LTE gas, for masers and for conjugate gas. tldr: The paper derives exact linear relations (sum rules) among the optical depths of OH doublet quartet transitions without invoking the Rayleigh-Jeans approximation, and proposes them as a tool for measuring variations of fundamental constants.
motivation: Existing OH sum-rule analyses rely on the Rayleigh-Jeans approximation, which limits their accuracy; the authors seek an exact, approximation-free relation valid across LTE, non-LTE, masing, and conjugate gas regimes.
method: Using catalogued Einstein A coefficients, they compute reduced transition dipole moments and show that every velocity channel of an OH doublet quartet satisfies an exact linear relation, with the 2Pi_1/2 J=1/2 level treated as the sole exception due to its forbidden line.

title: One-dimensional Second-gradient Elasticity: Pantograph-inspired Energies And Solitary Waves
authors: R. S. Hallyburton, I. Giorgio, C. Rodriguez
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a self-contained formulation of longitudinal motion in one-dimensional second-gradient continua. Starting from finite-strain kinematics, we then apply the Principle of Virtual Power to identify the governing field equation and contact actions, derive the balance laws, and establish the mechanical-energy identity for hyperelastic materials. Motivated by pantographic microstructures, we study a class of finite-strain energies formulated in terms of normalized strain measures and deformation-dependent strain-gradient moduli. For the associated equation of motion, a traveling-wave first integral yields a turning-point criterion for the existence of solitary waves with positive stretch, exponential decay, and finite mechanical energy, as well as uniqueness at each fixed speed within a prescribed strain interval. For suitable spring energies, a change of strain variable reduces this integral to a polynomial equation, yielding explicit tensile and compressive profiles for Green--Lagrange and Hencky strains under appropriate parameter and kinematic conditions. Under the positivity condition on the quartic potential, the constructed Hencky energy has several physically natural properties: it is nonnegative, admits the natural state as its unique zero and global minimizer, has a positive linearized modulus, penalizes stretch gradients, and diverges under both material collapse and unlimited extension. Furthermore, the stored energy is coercive with respect to the [MATH] norm of logarithmic strain. Together with mechanical-energy conservation, this yields uniform upper and positive lower bounds on stretch throughout the lifespan of smooth solutions. The theory's accessible mechanical origin, relatively simple mathematical foundation, and diverse solitary waves offer a tractable entry point to studying the rich nonlinear dispersive equations governing higher-gradient elastic continua.
tldr: The paper formulates one-dimensional second-gradient elasticity for pantograph-inspired continua and constructs solitary-wave solutions under finite-strain energies.
motivation: Pantographic microstructures motivate higher-gradient continuum models, but tractable one-dimensional formulations with explicit solitary-wave solutions are useful for understanding nonlinear dispersive behavior in such materials.
method: The authors derive the governing field equation via the Principle of Virtual Power, establish balance laws and a mechanical-energy identity, and analyze traveling-wave first integrals for finite-strain second-gradient energies.
result: They obtain turning-point criteria for solitary waves with positive stretch, exponential decay, and finite energy, and derive explicit tensile and compressive profiles for suitable Green-Lagrange and Hencky strain energies.
conclusion: The theory provides a mechanically grounded and mathematically accessible framework for higher-gradient elastic continua and their nonlinear solitary-wave dynamics.

title: Ratchet Effects For Swarmalators On Asymmetric Substrates
authors: B. Albert, A. Libal, C. J. O. Reichhardt, C. Reichhardt
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Swarmalators are particles which have internal degrees of freedom in the form of phase oscillators that can synchronize and change the dynamics of the particles. We explore the active matter disk swarmalator model proposed by Adorj\'{a}ni [Phys. Rev. E 109, 024607 (2024)] where there is an additional attraction or repulsion determined by whether the phases of particles within a certain radius synchronize or anti-synchronize. This model in the absence of swarmalator rules forms a motility-induced phase-separated (MIPS) state at high activity, but when the swarmalator rules are present, a number of additional states appear including an active gel, labyrinth state, frustrated MIPS, and frustrated fluid states. Here we examine ratchet effects for the Adorj\'{a}ni model coupled to asymmetric substrates. We find that swarmalator interactions can strongly enhance or suppress active matter ratcheting depending on the structural state of the system, and show that the ratchet efficiency depends on the substrate strength, substrate lattice spacing, and the motor force on the particles. The gel state exhibits the weakest ratcheting for small substrate spacing and can even produce a reversed ratchet motion, but shows the strongest ratcheting for large motor forces. The labyrinth state exhibits the strongest ratcheting over a wide range of parameters since the quasi-one-dimensional labyrinth morphology can match the substrate geometry well.
tldr: A numerical study of ratchet effects in an active-matter disk swarmalator model coupled to asymmetric periodic substrates.
motivation: Swarmalators—particles with internal phase-oscillator degrees of freedom that synchronize—produce rich collective states (active gel, labyrinth, frustrated MIPS), but their transport behavior on structured substrates has not been characterized.
method: Simulations of the Adorjáni swarmalator model on asymmetric substrates, scanning substrate strength, lattice spacing, and motor force to measure ratchet efficiency and directionality across structural states.
result: Swarmalator interactions can strongly enhance or suppress ratcheting depending on the emergent state; the gel state gives weakest (occasionally reversed) ratcheting at small spacing but strongest at large motor force, while the labyrinth state ratchets most strongly over a wide parameter range.
conclusion: Collective synchronization-driven morphology controls rectification of active motion, offering a knob for designing active-matter transport on asymmetric substrates.

title: Exact $l^2$ Convergence Through The Wavelet And Tent Space Characterizations Of $h^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $0<p\le 1$
authors: Mohamed El Aoumari
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the wavelet and tent space characterization of [MATH] to [MATH] via a local dyadic tent space [MATH], and derive the unconditional [MATH]-convergence of the resulting atomic decomposition, with an exact error identity refining Ding, Jiang and Zhu (2019).
tldr: The paper extends wavelet and tent-space characterizations of Hardy-type spaces to the local Hardy space h^p(R^n) for 0<p<=1, yielding an unconditional l^2-convergent atomic decomposition with an exact error identity.
motivation: Characterizations of classical Hardy spaces H^p via wavelets and tent spaces are well developed, but the local Hardy space h^p and the precise convergence/error behavior of the induced atomic decompositions remain incompletely understood.
method: The author introduces a local dyadic tent space adapted to h^p and proves wavelet and tent-space characterizations, then uses these to construct an atomic decomposition and analyze its l^2 convergence and error.
result: An unconditional l^2-convergence theorem for the atomic decomposition in h^p(R^n), together with an exact error identity that refines earlier work of Ding, Jiang and Zhu (2019).
conclusion: The results provide a sharp functional-analytic framework for local Hardy spaces via dyadic tent spaces, but the work is purely mathematical harmonic analysis with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum hardware.

title: Algebraic Properties Of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel Operators
authors: Kritika Babbar, Satyabrata Majee, Amit Maji
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of [MATH]---the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space [MATH]. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators under certain conditions. As applications, we describe the non-uniqueness of a decomposition [MATH], show that self-adjoint operators admit self-adjoint decompositions, give a necessary and sufficient inclusion criterion for [MATH] when [MATH] is a finite Blaschke product, and, from a first-order commutator characterization of [MATH], describe the products of its elements and the operators commuting with [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies algebraic properties of the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators on model spaces and characterizes intersections, decompositions, inclusions, products, and commutants.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the algebraic structure of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators, extending the theory of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators on model spaces.
method: They use operator-theoretic and complex-analytic techniques on model spaces, including commutator characterizations and finite Blaschke product conditions, to analyze the class and its intersection with related operator classes.
result: They characterize non-uniqueness of decompositions, show self-adjoint operators admit self-adjoint decompositions, give a necessary and sufficient inclusion criterion for finite Blaschke products, and describe products and commuting operators via a first-order commutator characterization.
conclusion: The work provides a structural algebraic analysis of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators, with applications to decomposition and inclusion properties on model spaces.

title: Character Cyclic Amenability Of Banach Algebras
authors: Hamid Sadeghi Nahrekhalaji
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the notion of character cyclic amenability for Banach algebras, which combines the cyclicity condition on derivations with the character-dependent module structure arising in character amenability. We establish several basic properties of this notion and investigate its behavior under standard Banach algebra constructions. In particular, we study character cyclic amenability for opposite algebras, projective tensor products, l1-direct sums, quotient algebras, dense homomorphic images, and theta-Lau products. We also provide examples illustrating the relationship between character cyclic amenability and other amenability-type properties, including examples showing that character cyclic amenability does not imply cyclic amenability. Finally, we characterize character cyclic amenability for module extension Banach algebras in terms of phi-cyclic derivations and derivations associated with the underlying Banach module.
tldr: The paper introduces and studies character cyclic amenability for Banach algebras, a purely functional-analytic cohomological property combining character-dependent module structures with cyclic derivations.
motivation: Character amenability and cyclic amenability are well-established amenability-type notions in Banach algebra theory; the authors seek a unified notion that incorporates both the character-dependent module structure and the cyclicity condition on derivations.
method: The authors define character cyclic amenability via phi-cyclic derivations into dual modules, then establish permanence properties under opposite algebras, projective tensor products, l1-direct sums, quotients, dense homomorphic images, and theta-Lau products, and characterize the property for module extension algebras.
result: Basic hereditary properties are proven, examples separate character cyclic amenability from ordinary cyclic amenability, and a characterization of character cyclic amenability for module extension Banach algebras is obtained in terms of phi-cyclic derivations and derivations tied to the underlying Banach module.
conclusion: Character cyclic amenability is a well-behaved but strictly weaker variant of cyclic amenability, with structural results paralleling classical amenability theory in abstract harmonic analysis.

title: Bornologies And Kuratowski-Painlev\'e Convergence To The Empty Set Revisited
authors: Gerald Beer Basile Beyer de Ryke
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a noncompact metrizable space and let [MATH] be a sequence of nonempty closed sets converging to the empty set in the sense of Kuratowski--Painlev\'e. The subsets of [MATH] whose closures meet at most finitely many terms form a bornology [MATH]. We give an internal criterion for inclusion between two such bornologies and recover each of them from a canonical free filter of closed sets. In fact, a nontrivial bornology is sequence-induced exactly when it has the enlargement property and its closed polar has countable character. Our principal result says that the bornology of relatively compact sets is sequence-induced precisely when [MATH] is locally compact and separable; in the locally compact case the character of its closed polar is the density of [MATH]. In the penultimate section, we make a clever use of the sequence [MATH] in the real line to give a negative answer to a conjecture posed in 2001 about a coarsest topology making the associated bornology a nontrivial metric bornology. Finally, we end the paper with a more general result: a coarsest such supertopology exists if and only if the original topology already makes the induced bornology a nontrivial metric bornology, in which case the coarsest supertopology is the original topology itself.
tldr: This pure topology paper studies bornologies induced by sequences of closed sets converging to the empty set in the Kuratowski-Painlevé sense.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize sequence-induced bornologies, recover them from canonical free filters, and resolve a 2001 conjecture about coarsest topologies making such bornologies metric.
method: They use bornology theory, Kuratowski-Painlevé convergence, closed polars, and topological cardinal invariants such as density and character.
result: They give an internal inclusion criterion, show the relatively compact bornology is sequence-induced exactly when the space is locally compact and separable, and disprove the 2001 conjecture via an example on the real line.
conclusion: The paper provides a general topological characterization of coarsest supertopologies yielding nontrivial metric bornologies, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Closed Lindel\"of $\Sigma$ Kernels Of Neighborhood Assignments In Charming Spaces
authors: Xing-Yu Hu

motivation: The work addresses open questions in set-theoretic topology concerning neighborhood assignments, kernels, and the Lindelöf property in charming spaces, aiming to characterize L-space-type conditions.
method: Purely topological/transfinite combinatorial arguments: kernel constructions, closed discrete sets, continuous closed surjections, and a transfinite closed-core iteration of the Hu–Yin boundary reduction with sharpness constructions.
result: Establishes existence of countable Lindelöf-closed kernels, an exact one-step formulation of the remaining L-space problem, a lifting equivalence for closed surjections, and a sharp stabilization bound for the transfinite iteration.

title: On The Frieze Patterns By Conway And Coxeter
authors: Pavel Tumarkin Anna Felikson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The story of frieze patterns started in 1970s with a paper by Coxeter and two short papers by Conway and Coxeter, one listing questions and the other providing brief answers. During the first three decades it was followed by only a handful of papers observing some further properties of the same objects. Then Propp (2005) and Caldero and Chapoton (2006) established connections between frieze patterns and the recent theory of cluster algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky in early 2000s. Since then the theory of frieze patterns exploded with new results, and frieze patterns found a wide spectrum of connections in various domains of mathematics, including combinatorics, geometry, representation theory and integrable systems. The literature on frieze patterns grew vastly and continues to expand. In this note we give a brief overview of some of the directions emerging from the papers by Conway and Coxeter and single out core ideas which were later replayed in different contexts.
tldr: A brief overview of frieze patterns introduced by Conway and Coxeter and their later connections to cluster algebras and other areas of mathematics.
motivation: The paper aims to survey the development of frieze pattern theory from its origins in the work of Conway and Coxeter through its modern connections with cluster algebras, combinatorics, geometry, representation theory, and integrable systems.
method: The authors provide a conceptual overview of key directions and core ideas emerging from the original papers, organizing later developments and connections rather than presenting new technical results.
result: The note identifies central themes in frieze pattern theory and traces how they have been replayed and generalized in subsequent mathematical contexts.
conclusion: Frieze patterns have become a rich mathematical subject with broad interdisciplinary connections, but this survey is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Stability Of Doubly Indexed Discrete Linear Systems
authors: Tyler Mcmillen Alain Bourget
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stability of the two-dimensional discrete dynamical system defined by \[ x_{i,j} = A x_{i-1,j} + B x_{i,j-1},\] where [MATH]. Although this system, commonly known as the Fornasini-Marchesini model, has been examined for decades, several key stability results have lacked rigorous proofs. This paper establishes precise and self-contained criteria for Lyapunov, asymptotic, and neutral stability under general bounded boundary conditions. In particular, we prove that asymptotic stability is equivalent to the spectral condition [MATH] for all [MATH]. We further analyze the commutative case, derive recurrence relations for anti-diagonal sums, and present new examples and counterexamples illustrating the nuances of stability. The results are complemented by sufficient conditions based on matrix norms, Lyapunov functions, and the joint spectral radius.
tldr: The paper gives rigorous, self-contained stability criteria (Lyapunov, asymptotic, neutral) for the two-dimensional discrete Fornasini-Marchesini linear system under general bounded boundary conditions.
motivation: Although the Fornasini-Marchesini model has been studied for decades, several of its key stability results lacked rigorous proofs, so the authors aim to close this gap.
method: They prove equivalence of asymptotic stability to a spectral condition over the bidisc, analyze the commutative case, derive recurrence relations for anti-diagonal sums, and supplement the analysis with matrix-norm, Lyapunov-function, and joint-spectral-radius sufficient conditions.
result: Precise stability criteria are established, including the equivalence of asymptotic stability with the spectral condition for all points in the relevant domain, along with new examples and counterexamples illustrating subtle stability behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for stability analysis of 2D discrete linear systems, but it lies entirely within classical control/dynamical-systems mathematics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Kwapie\'n's Property (k) In Lipschitz-free Spaces
authors: Jerzy K\k{a}kol Tomasz Kania
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a Lipschitz-free space [MATH] fails Kwapie\'n's property (K) whenever its underlying metric space [MATH] contains a bi-Lipschitz copy of [MATH], where [MATH] is closed with positive measure and [MATH] contains a Cantor metric space. Consequently, this holds for every subset of [MATH], [MATH], whose closure has positive measure, and for a compact planar set of Assouad dimension one. These Lipschitz-free spaces embed into no strongly weakly compactly generated space and no [MATH]-space; in the separable case their duals are not isomorphic to [MATH]. Combining our result with a decomposition of Aliaga and Medina, we show that [MATH] is strongly weakly compactly generated if and only if it has (K), and this occurs precisely when [MATH]. In particular, [MATH] does not embed isomorphically into [MATH], answering a question of Aliaga. The planar examples nevertheless have the Dunford--Pettis property and Pe{\l}czy\'nski's property [MATH] and are weakly sequentially complete.

motivation: Kwapień's property (K) and strongly weakly compactly generated (SWCG) spaces are central notions in the isomorphic theory of Banach spaces, and the structure of Lipschitz-free spaces remains poorly understood; the authors aim to settle when these properties hold, in particular answering a question of Aliaga.
method: The authors use bi-Lipschitz embeddings, measure-theoretic arguments on closed positive-measure sets containing Cantor sets, and a decomposition of Aliaga and Medina to link property (K) with strong weak compact generation of Lipschitz-free spaces.
result: They show that F(M) fails property (K) whenever M contains a bi-Lipschitz copy of such a set, deduce that the corresponding Lipschitz-free spaces embed into no SWCG space and no l1-space, and prove that F(M) is SWCG if and only if it has (K), precisely when M is a specific degenerate case, thereby showing F(R) does not embed isomorphically into F(R^2).
conclusion: The paper establishes broad classes of metric spaces whose Lipschitz-free spaces lack property (K) and are not SWCG, while noting that the planar examples retain the Dunford-Pettis property, Pełczyński's property (V), and weak sequential completeness.

title: Monte Carlo Power Iteration Algorithms: Convergence, Analysis And Application To Reactor Criticality Calculations
authors: Alexander M. G. Cox, Tom Davis, Julian Hofstadler, Andreas E. Kyprianou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms in the context of reactor criticality simulations. Under mild conditions on the underlying physical system and the algorithmic structure, we derive explicit error bounds, which are to the best of our knowledge the first rigorous results for such methods which are ubiquitous in nuclear engineering. This is done by exploiting connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms, and extending recent developments about stochastic neutron transport. We demonstrate the applicability of our results by considering a concrete version of the Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm as well as variance reduction schemes.
tldr: The paper develops rigorous error bounds for Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms used in reactor criticality simulations by connecting them to sequential Monte Carlo and stochastic neutron transport.
motivation: Monte Carlo power iteration is widely used in nuclear engineering for reactor criticality calculations, but rigorous convergence and error analysis have been lacking.
method: The authors exploit connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms and recent results on stochastic neutron transport to derive explicit error bounds under mild physical and algorithmic assumptions.
result: They obtain first rigorous error bounds for such methods, demonstrate applicability to a concrete Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm, and consider variance reduction schemes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for Monte Carlo power iteration in reactor criticality simulations, but it is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Building Mathematical Software -- Lessons From The Development Of Gap
authors: Alexander Hulpke
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematical software has particular needs that are not all covered by the existing literature on software engineering or algorithm design. This paper looks at some of these aspects, in the concrete context of the computer algebra system GAP. It also studies the potential impact AI systems could have on the development process for mathematical software.
tldr: A reflective essay on the engineering practices and requirements specific to mathematical software, drawn from the development of the GAP computer algebra system, with speculation on how AI could reshape that process.
motivation: Mathematical software has needs (correctness, abstraction, long-term maintenance, community-driven design) that standard software-engineering and algorithm-design literature does not fully address, so the author aims to articulate these gaps.
method: Qualitative case-study discussion based on the author's experience maintaining and developing GAP, combined with commentary on the possible role of AI-assisted development.
result: Identifies distinctive aspects of mathematical software development — such as verified mathematical semantics, deep abstraction hierarchies, and distributed expert communities — and argues that AI tools could assist but must respect these constraints.
conclusion: The paper offers practical lessons for developers of mathematical software and flags open questions about integrating AI into such workflows; it contains no physics or information-theoretic content.

title: Variations Of The Harmonic Entropy And Linear Drift On Negatively Curved Surfaces
authors: Karen Butt, Alena Erchenko, Tristan Humbert
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.
tldr: The paper computes derivatives of the harmonic entropy of geodesic flows and of the linear drift of Brownian motion on closed negatively curved surfaces under conformal deformations, and derives monotonicity along normalized Ricci flow.
motivation: Harmonic entropy and linear drift are geometric-dynamical invariants whose behaviour under deformation of the metric is not well understood; the authors aim to relate them to Liouville entropy and curvature.
method: Analytic computation of first variations of harmonic entropy and linear drift for conformal families of negatively curved metrics, combined with comparison arguments under the normalized Ricci flow.
result: Harmonic entropy is strictly decreasing and linear drift strictly increasing along normalized Ricci flow for non-constant negative curvature; hyperbolic metrics admit a conformal neighbourhood where linear drift is bounded below by Liouville entropy with equality only for hyperbolic metrics.
conclusion: The work establishes new monotonicity and comparison results linking thermodynamically flavoured dynamical invariants to curvature, but remains within pure geometry/dynamical systems.

title: Quasi-periodic Tree Sets And Structure Trees
authors: Mikael Pichot
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We expand our discussion of the almost stability theorem of Dicks and Dunwoody in the context of probability measure preserving equivalence relations.
tldr: The paper extends the Dicks–Dunwoody almost stability theorem to the setting of probability measure preserving equivalence relations using quasi-periodic tree sets and structure trees.
motivation: The work aims to broaden the scope of the almost stability theorem, a tool from geometric group theory, to measurable equivalence relations arising in ergodic theory and measured group theory.
method: It develops quasi-periodic tree sets and structure trees as analogues of the classical Bass–Serre / Dicks–Dunwoody machinery in the context of probability measure preserving equivalence relations.
result: The paper establishes a version of the almost stability theorem applicable to such equivalence relations, likely yielding structural decompositions via trees or tree sets.
conclusion: The results contribute to measured group theory and geometric group theory but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hybridizing 0/1 Knapsack And Priority-Aware Tsp For Vehicle Routing: An Applied Variant Of The Tsp With Profits
authors: Francisco M\'arcio Barboza Aron Da Silva Bezerra
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distribution logistics with capacity constraints and service priorities can be modeled as a variant of the (TSPP), in which not all customers need to be visited and the selection of which customers to serve is part of the problem. This paper proposes an applied variant with two adaptations: (i) a 0/1 Knapsack objective function weighted by client priority squared ([MATH]), and (ii) a priority bias in the Nearest Neighbor heuristic for the TSP, parameterized by [MATH]. The approach is evaluated on a scenario with 14 customers and a 1,100~kg capacity, complemented by a comparative experimental protocol against the classical greedy heuristic ([MATH] ordering) and an integer programming solver. Results on the base scenario show 9 customers served, 96.4\% capacity utilization, and R\$~18,392.60 revenue, with all 5 excluded customers being low-priority. A sensitivity analysis of the priority exponent justifies the quadratic choice. The limitations of the hierarchical decomposition are explicitly discussed.
tldr: The paper proposes a classical vehicle-routing variant combining a priority-weighted 0/1 knapsack objective with a priority-biased nearest-neighbor heuristic for the traveling salesman problem with profits.
motivation: Distribution logistics with capacity constraints and service priorities can be modeled as a TSP with profits, where selecting which customers to serve is part of the optimization problem.
method: The authors adapt the TSP with profits using a quadratic client-priority-weighted 0/1 knapsack objective and a parameterized priority bias in the nearest-neighbor heuristic, evaluated against a greedy heuristic and an integer programming solver on a 14-customer scenario.
result: In the base scenario, the method serves 9 customers with 96.4% capacity utilization and R$18,392.60 revenue, excluding only low-priority customers; a sensitivity analysis supports the quadratic priority exponent.
conclusion: The hierarchical decomposition is useful for the applied routing scenario, but its limitations are explicitly discussed.

title: A Homological Approach To Dynamics
authors: William Kalies, Konstantin Mischaikow, Robert Vandervorst
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note describes a novel approach to systematically characterize dynamics based on finite information. We present an algebraic framework for dynamics from which it is possible to deduce more traditional descriptors associated with the qualitative structures of the geometric theory of dynamical systems. The purpose of this paper is to indicate how this approach can be used to obtain interpretable characterizations of dynamics that are robust with respect to perturbations, in the context of models of multiscale and data-driven systems.
tldr: The paper introduces an algebraic/homological framework that extracts robust, interpretable descriptors of dynamical systems from finite information.
motivation: Traditional geometric descriptors of dynamics are sensitive to perturbations and hard to compute from finite or noisy data, motivating a more robust algebraic characterization.
method: The authors build a homological-algebraic formalism for dynamics and show it recovers classical qualitative descriptors, aimed at multiscale and data-driven models.
result: The framework yields interpretable, perturbation-robust characterizations of dynamical behavior derived from finite data.
conclusion: The approach offers a systematic algebraic route to dynamical descriptors suitable for data-driven and multiscale systems.

title: Periodic Solutions And Exponential Attractivity In Hopfield-Type Neural Networks With Generalized Piecewise Constant Arguments: Impulsive And Nonimpulsive Cases
authors: Samuel Castillo Apolonio Ricardo Torres Naranjo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate an impulsive Hopfield-type neural network with a generalized piecewise constant argument, including the nonimpulsive case in which all jump terms vanish. The piecewise constant argument is given by [MATH] on each interval [MATH], where [MATH], [MATH]. Depending on the position of [MATH], the argument may be advanced, retarded, or of mixed type. By representing periodic solutions through a Green function and applying a fixed-point argument, we obtain explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an [MATH]-periodic solution. We then use a Gronwall-type estimate, together with period averages, to prove that this solution is globally exponentially attractive. These conditions can be checked directly from the system parameters, without requiring explicit knowledge of the periodic solution. In the course of the analysis, we also revisit and correct some estimates presented by Pinto et al. . The case [MATH] reduces to their setting, whereas our results cover the more general choice of [MATH] within each interval. We also present examples illustrating different types of piecewise constant arguments.
tldr: The paper studies existence, uniqueness, and global exponential attractivity of periodic solutions in impulsive Hopfield-type neural networks with generalized piecewise constant arguments.
motivation: Hopfield-type neural networks with piecewise constant arguments can exhibit advanced, retarded, or mixed dynamics, and prior results by Pinto et al. are limited to a special case and contain estimates needing correction.
method: The authors represent periodic solutions via a Green function, apply a fixed-point argument for existence and uniqueness, and use a Gronwall-type estimate with period averages to prove global exponential attractivity.
result: They obtain explicit sufficient conditions verifiable directly from system parameters, without requiring explicit knowledge of the periodic solution, and they correct earlier estimates while extending results to a more general piecewise constant argument.
conclusion: The work provides general sufficient conditions for periodic solutions and exponential attractivity in impulsive and nonimpulsive Hopfield-type networks, illustrated with examples for different piecewise constant argument types.

title: Count-catcher: Lean Theorems From Model Counting Certificates
authors: Stefan Szeider Johannes K. Fichte
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present count-catcher, a tool that turns a CPOG certificate of a count by the exact model counter d4 into a Lean theorem that a CNF formula defined in Lean has exactly N models over V variables. With an encoding lemma, this theorem becomes a theorem about the number of combinatorial objects. A CPOG certificate consists of a Boolean circuit equivalent to the formula and a proof of equivalence. count-catcher checks in Lean that the formula implies the circuit (forward check) and the circuit implies the formula (reverse check). For the forward check, lrat-catcher streams a refutation through the LRAT checker of Lean's standard library. The reverse check and the validity check of the circuit are computations proved correct in Lean. Lean runs all three checks as compiled code, so the theorem depends on Lean's kernel, compiler and runtime, as does CPOG's verified checker. We combine the theorem with results from Mathlib, for instance with Burnside's lemma to count graphs up to isomorphism. We prove the number of Latin squares of order 8 as a weighted sum of hundreds of certified counts from about eight terabytes of certificates. We turn about half of the 2022 Model Counting Competition formulas into theorems, with the three checks taking about a quarter of the time of CPOG's verified checker. We found that CPOG's unverified checker reported wrong counts, and removed its verified checker's dependence on two unproved lemmas. End to end, a theorem costs about the same as a checked count.
tldr: The count-catcher tool converts exact model-counting certificates (CPOG) into verified Lean theorems about the number of models of CNF formulas and of combinatorial objects such as Latin squares of order 8.
motivation: Exact model counters produce counts, but trusting them requires either unverified checkers or expensive verified checkers; a machine-checkable proof object tying counts to formal theorems would make such results trustworthy and reusable in mathematics libraries.
method: count-catcher takes a CPOG certificate (a Boolean circuit equivalent to the formula plus an equivalence proof) and performs three Lean checks: a forward implication via an LRAT refutation streamed through Lean's standard-library LRAT checker, and reverse-implication and circuit-validity checks as computations proved correct in Lean, all run as compiled code.
result: About half of the 2022 Model Counting Competition formulas were turned into Lean theorems at roughly a quarter of the runtime of CPOG's verified checker, the number of Latin squares of order 8 was proved as a weighted sum of hundreds of certified counts from ~8 TB of certificates, and CPOG's unverified checker was found to report wrong counts while two unproved lemmas were removed from its verified checker.
conclusion: End-to-end, a formal theorem costs about the same as a checked count, providing a practical route to kernel-verified combinatorial enumeration.

title: Bringing Hardware Security Education To All: A Seamless Curriculum Integration Approach
authors: Tanvir Hossain, Mahmudul Hasan, Kareem El-Araby, Lorenzo R. Godinez, Swarup Bhunia, Md Tauhidur Rahman, Tamzidul Hoque
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cybersecurity education has predominantly focused on software and network security, under the assumption that the underlying hardware is trustworthy. Threats introduced through the global semiconductor supply chain, together with vulnerabilities arising during design and integration, challenge the assumption that hardware can serve as an unquestioned root of trust. Sensor-enabled systems and machine-learning accelerators further expand the hardware attack surface. The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. At the University of Florida, fewer than 7% of the undergraduate electrical and computer engineering students register for the introductory HS course each year. We present an integrated and economical approach that disseminates fundamental HS concepts within existing core courses through contextual learning. Nine hands-on modules were developed such that each security concept exercises an associated design concept of the core course, as a component of that course and not as a course of their own. Doing the security work is how the student exercises the design topic, so the modules are built to strengthen the host course and not only to add to it. Three were assessed across three offerings of the embedded systems course through one course survey and two conducted by an external evaluator, with 25 respondents. We report what those instruments measured and the limitations of the approach.
tldr: The paper presents nine hands-on modules that embed hardware security concepts into existing undergraduate electrical/computer engineering core courses rather than offering standalone electives.
motivation: Cybersecurity curricula focus on software and network security while assuming hardware is trustworthy, yet supply-chain threats and ML accelerator vulnerabilities expand the hardware attack surface; dedicated hardware security courses are scarce and elective, with fewer than 7% of UF undergraduates enrolling.
method: A contextual-learning approach integrates security exercises into the design content of host courses; three modules were assessed across three offerings of an embedded systems course via one course survey and two external-evaluator instruments with 25 respondents.
result: The assessment instruments measured gains in student awareness and engagement with hardware security concepts within the core course, and the authors discuss the limitations of the integration approach.
conclusion: Economical curriculum integration can broaden hardware security education to all students, though the evidence base is small and further evaluation is needed.

title: The Complexity Of Strategizing Against No-Regret Learners: Pure When It Is Easy, Hard Even When Mixed
authors: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis Yiheng Su
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the computational complexity of clairvoyant strategy optimization against a known online learner in finite-horizon repeated games. In general-sum games with bounded payoffs, unless [MATH], no polynomial-time optimizer can achieve a reward within [MATH] of the reward of the optimal pure-action sequence for an absolute constant [MATH], even when allowed to output explicitly represented mixed strategies at every round. Our hardness result strengthens prior work along two complementary axes: it extends to a broader class of learning dynamics, including widely used mean-based algorithms, answering an open question of Assos, Dagan, and Rajaraman (2025) for learners beyond multiplicative weights; and it permits mixed outputs while retaining the weaker pure-sequence benchmark. Thus, neither mixed strategies nor algorithmic specificity removes the computational obstruction in general-sum games. In sharp contrast, zero-sum games exhibit the reverse phenomenon: deterministic pure actions suffice for efficiently recovering the leading surplus guarantees previously obtained through mixed play against Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) opponents. Thus, the two regimes form a striking mirror image: mixed play cannot overcome general-sum hardness even against a pure benchmark, whereas pure play retains the full surplus guarantees of mixed strategies in zero-sum games.
tldr: The paper studies the computational complexity of clairvoyantly optimizing against no-regret learners in repeated games, showing general-sum hardness persists even with mixed strategies while zero-sum games admit efficient pure-action recovery.
motivation: It addresses an open question on whether mixed strategies or broader mean-based learners can overcome computational obstructions in strategizing against known online learners.
method: The authors prove hardness results for general-sum games against a broader class of learning dynamics and derive efficient pure-action guarantees for zero-sum games against FTRL learners.
result: In general-sum games, no polynomial-time optimizer can match the optimal pure-action sequence unless certain complexity assumptions fail, even with mixed outputs; in zero-sum games, deterministic pure actions suffice to recover leading surplus guarantees.
conclusion: The two regimes form a mirror image: mixed play cannot overcome general-sum hardness, whereas pure play retains full surplus guarantees in zero-sum settings.

title: PHP2Shell And The Future Of AI-Discovered Vulnerability Disclosure: Evidence, Verification, And Human Authority
authors: Asadullah Abdullah Khan Toqeer Ali Syed
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery can produce technically plausible findings faster than maintainers can validate, coordinate, and safely disclose them. The resulting challenge is not only to establish whether a vulnerability claim is credible, but also to ensure that its supporting evidence, human authorization, intended recipients, and applicable policy remain bound to the same case revision. We present FedTrust-CVDv2, a federated coordinated vulnerability disclosure framework that separates evidence validation, interorganizational coordination, human governance, and permissioned auditing. The framework binds independently signed observations to exact evidence revisions and scopes external actions to approved payloads, audiences, expiry, policy, and revocation state while preserving existing CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) roles. A local reference implementation accepted all 25 valid fixtures and rejected all 650 invalid fixtures across 27 constructed policy families; six single-safeguard ablations admitted 25-75 invalid fixtures. Supporting experiments exercised signed messaging, authenticated encryption, audit certificates, and finite quorum-set conditions. A PHP2Shell case formulation illustrates how runtime evidence, patch state, emergency coordination, and CNA authority can be represented without attributing unsupported claims to AI or treating audit integrity as vulnerability truth. This short version focuses on the architecture, evidence-to-action contract, selected conformance results, and case formulation. An expanded version containing the full implementation, extended experiments, operational analysis, and additional results will be submitted to a journal.
tldr: The paper presents FedTrust-CVDv2, a federated coordinated vulnerability disclosure framework for binding AI-assisted vulnerability evidence, human authorization, recipients, and policy to a specific case revision.
motivation: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery can generate plausible claims faster than maintainers can validate, coordinate, and safely disclose them, creating a need for evidence-bound and governance-aware disclosure workflows.
method: The authors propose a federated CVD architecture separating evidence validation, interorganizational coordination, human governance, and permissioned auditing, and test a local reference implementation against valid and invalid fixtures across constructed policy families.
result: The implementation accepted all 25 valid fixtures and rejected all 650 invalid fixtures across 27 policy families, while single-safeguard ablations admitted 25-75 invalid fixtures; additional experiments exercised signed messaging, authenticated encryption, audit certificates, and quorum conditions.
conclusion: The framework illustrates how runtime evidence, patch state, emergency coordination, and CNA authority can be represented without conflating audit integrity with vulnerability truth, though the short version focuses on architecture and selected conformance results.

title: A Simple Presentation Of Robust Membership Inference Attacks
authors: Renaud Gaucher, Ephraim Linder, Adam Smith, Jonathan Ullman, Lydia Zakynthinou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a membership inference attack, an attacker is given the data of a particular individual, and tries to determine if that individual was included in a particular dataset, given some kind of statistics derived from the dataset or a model trained on the dataset. Roughly, a membership inference attack is robust if it succeeds even when the statistics are highly noisy, regardless of how that noise is introduced. We give a simple presentation of robust membership inference attacks for mean estimation, covering both multivariate Gaussian distributions and binary product distributions. We also give a summary of the literature on robust membership inference, covering history, extensions, and connections to other research areas.
tldr: A tutorial-style presentation of robust membership inference attacks for mean estimation under multivariate Gaussian and binary product distributions, plus a literature survey.
motivation: Membership inference attacks are a core privacy risk for statistical and machine-learning releases; robustness against arbitrary noise injection is needed to guarantee privacy even for very noisy statistics.
method: The authors give a simplified exposition of robust membership inference tests for mean estimation, treating both multivariate Gaussian data and binary product distributions, and survey the literature on robust membership inference.
result: The paper provides accessible derivations of the attack's guarantees under heavy noise and situates prior work, extensions, and connections to adjacent areas of privacy research.
conclusion: The work is an expository and survey contribution to classical data-privacy theory, aimed at making robust membership inference more widely understandable.

title: Noise Shapes The Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners
authors: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis Yiheng Su
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work has shown that, in zero-sum games, an optimizer can extract [MATH] strategic surplus---cumulative payoff above the minimax benchmark---against noiseless no-regret learners with a constant step size. However, in practice, learners often act on perturbed payoff scores and use decaying learning rates [MATH]. Since existing extraction mechanisms rely on exact scores, a natural question is whether noise shields the learner from exploitation and eliminates surplus altogether. We address this question for the widely used class of Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) algorithms. Under standard regularity conditions, we establish three results, none of which assumes independence of the noise. First, under summability conditions, passive play of a strategy fixed independently of the horizon earns at most constant surplus. Second, we design a new mechanism that exploits the learner's noise-dependent response: a clairvoyant optimizer who knows the update rule and the limiting mean response secures [MATH] surplus whenever that mean is profitable. Third, even when that mean is not profitable, active alternating play extracts [MATH] surplus by exploiting the learner's movement rather than its location, under suitable responsiveness and stability conditions. Finally, at the canonical learning rate [MATH], we recover the noiseless [MATH] rate for mean-zero, finite-variance perturbations---whether fresh with arbitrary temporal dependence or accumulated from i.i.d. increments---provided the limiting mean response is profitable.
tldr: This paper studies how payoff noise affects an optimizer's ability to extract strategic surplus against no-regret learners in zero-sum games.
motivation: Prior work showed that optimizers can exploit noiseless no-regret learners with constant step sizes, but practical learners use noisy payoff scores and decaying learning rates, raising the question of whether noise eliminates exploitability.
method: The authors analyze Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) learners under perturbed payoff scores without assuming independent noise, and design passive and active play mechanisms to extract surplus.
result: They show constant surplus under summability conditions for passive play, construct a clairvoyant mechanism achieving surplus when the limiting mean response is profitable, and show active alternating play can extract surplus even when the mean is not profitable; at a canonical learning rate they recover the noiseless rate for mean-zero finite-variance noise.
conclusion: Noise does not necessarily shield no-regret learners from exploitation; instead, the structure of noise shapes the optimizer's achievable surplus.

title: Impossibility Of No-Regret In Multi-Agent Bidding
authors: Zongjun Yang, Rachitesh Kumar, Christian Kroer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider [MATH] repeated second-price auctions across [MATH] pacing bidders with i.i.d. item arrivals, and show that it is computationally impossible for all bidders to achieve no-regret simultaneously while satisfying their respective budget or return-on-investment constraints. Therefore, in the prominent internet auction systems where buyers simultaneously deploy pacing algorithms or automated bidding agents, we cannot hope to achieve joint no-regret guarantees in general. We establish a deterministic relationship that high variance in online bidding systems implies high regret. By showing that one can extract a pacing equilibrium from a low-variance system, we prove PPAD-hardness of attaining joint no-regret. For several widely used bidding algorithms, we also show evidence from dynamical systems and numerical simulations that they can indeed display high-variance behavior through cycling, even on simple market instances.
tldr: The paper proves that in repeated second-price auctions with multiple pacing bidders, achieving joint no-regret while respecting budget/ROI constraints is computationally intractable (PPAD-hard), and that high regret is tied to high variance in bidding dynamics.
motivation: Internet ad auctions increasingly rely on automated pacing agents, so one would like to know whether such agents can simultaneously learn near-optimal strategies; the authors ask whether joint no-regret guarantees are achievable at all.
method: They establish a deterministic link between high variance in the bidding system and high regret, show that a low-variance system would yield a pacing equilibrium (giving PPAD-hardness of joint no-regret), and supplement this with dynamical-systems arguments and numerical simulations of common bidding algorithms.
result: Joint no-regret is computationally impossible in general, and several widely used pacing algorithms can exhibit persistent cycling and high-variance behavior even on simple market instances.
conclusion: Practitioners cannot expect universal joint no-regret guarantees from simultaneously deployed autobidding agents, and variance/cycling should be treated as intrinsic features of such multi-agent auction systems.

title: When Do Token Systems Stabilize? Compatibility Constraints And Community Structure
authors: Flore Sentenac, Mingwei Yang, Sophie H. Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Token systems support repeated service exchange without monetary transfers, but their viability depends on the stability of token balances. We study token systems with compatibility constraints among agents. A requester is randomly sampled in each period, and only a few randomly sampled agents are available to provide service. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition for stability and show that the minimum-token rule, which selects the available provider with the lowest token balance, achieves the optimal stability region. We then apply this stability criterion to a random token system generated from stochastic block models with uniformly sampled requesters. We tightly characterize the stability regime by identifying two obstructions to stability: insufficient service opportunities for a group of communities or for an individual agent.
tldr: The paper analyzes stability conditions for token-based service-exchange systems with compatibility constraints and community structure.
motivation: Token systems can support repeated service exchange without money, but their viability depends on whether token balances remain stable under random request and provider availability.
method: The authors derive a necessary and sufficient stability condition, prove optimality of the minimum-token provider-selection rule, and apply the criterion to random token systems generated from stochastic block models.
result: They characterize the optimal stability region and identify two obstructions to stability: insufficient service opportunities for a group of communities and for an individual agent.
conclusion: The work provides tight stability characterizations for token systems with compatibility constraints and community structure, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sensitivity Of Rms Delay Spread Estimation To Power Delay Profile Thresholding In Time-Varying Channels At 33 GHz
authors: Jaros{\l}aw Wojtu\'n, Bartosz Czaja, Tomasz Grasza, Jan M. Kelner, Cezary Zi\'o{\l}kowski, Radek Zavorka, Josef Vychodil, Tomas Mikulasek, Jiri Blumenstein, Ales Prokes, Aniruddha Chandra
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Root mean square (RMS) delay spread is a key parameter characterizing temporal dispersion in radio propagation channels. Its estimation from measured power delay profiles (PDPs), however, depends strongly on the adopted power threshold. This paper investigates the sensitivity of RMS delay spread estimates to relative PDP thresholding in a time-varying millimeter-wave channel at 33 GHz. The analysis uses wideband channel sounding measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment with moving vehicles. The temporal evolution and empirical cumulative distributions of RMS delay spread are evaluated for thresholds ranging from -20 to -50 dB. Reducing the threshold increases the median RMS delay spread from approximately 140 to 168 ns and the 90th percentile from 200 to 210 ns. Both statistics converge at lower thresholds, with -40 dB providing a practical convergence level. The results emphasize the importance of threshold selection for reliable channel characterization and consistent comparison of measurements.
tldr: This paper analyzes how relative power-delay-profile thresholding affects RMS delay spread estimates in a time-varying 33 GHz millimeter-wave channel.
motivation: RMS delay spread is an important radio-channel dispersion parameter, but its estimation depends strongly on the chosen PDP threshold, motivating a systematic sensitivity study.
method: Wideband channel sounding measurements in a dynamic road environment with moving vehicles are used to compute RMS delay spread statistics for thresholds from -20 dB to -50 dB.
result: Lowering the threshold increases the median RMS delay spread from about 140 ns to 168 ns and the 90th percentile from 200 ns to 210 ns, with convergence around -40 dB.
conclusion: Threshold choice materially affects RMS delay spread estimates, and -40 dB is suggested as a practical convergence level for reliable channel characterization and consistent comparisons.

title: Proximal Point Newton Methods For Nonconvex Optimization
authors: Shuzhong Zhang Chang He
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor methods offer improved complexity guarantees for nonconvex optimization, but evaluating high-order derivatives and solving the corresponding subproblems can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we develop a proximal point Newton framework that exploits third-derivative smoothness using only gradients and Hessians. Under Hessian Lipschitz continuity, a single-loop proximal point Newton method that alternates between negative-curvature directions and Newton steps finds an [MATH]-approximate second-order stationary point within [MATH] second-order oracle evaluations. When the third derivative is also Lipschitz continuous, we introduce an accelerated proximal point Newton method and obtain a dimension-free complexity of [MATH], matching that of the third-order tensor methods up to logarithmic factors without constructing tensors or solving tensor subproblems. We further develop an adaptive inexact Newton--CG variant that requires no prior knowledge of Lipschitz constants and preserves the improved oracle complexity with high probability. Under uniformly bounded queried Hessians, this variant achieves a Hessian-vector product complexity of [MATH], improving upon the previous [MATH] result attained by existing second-order methods such as cubic regularized Newton method and Newton--CG method. Preliminary numerical experiments are encouraging.
tldr: The paper develops proximal point Newton-type methods that attain third-order-tensor-level complexity for finding approximate second-order stationary points in nonconvex optimization using only gradient and Hessian information.
motivation: Tensor methods give better complexity guarantees for nonconvex optimization, but forming high-order derivatives and solving tensor subproblems is computationally prohibitive, motivating methods that mimic their guarantees with cheaper second-order oracles.
method: A single-loop proximal point Newton framework alternates negative-curvature steps with Newton steps under Hessian Lipschitz continuity, extended to an accelerated variant under third-derivative Lipschitz continuity and an adaptive inexact Newton-CG variant that avoids knowledge of Lipschitz constants.
result: The methods achieve dimension-free O(epsilon^{-3/2}) style complexity matching third-order tensor methods up to logarithmic factors, and the adaptive variant reaches an improved Hessian-vector product complexity of O(epsilon^{-7/4}) under bounded queried Hessians, with encouraging numerical experiments.
conclusion: Second-order proximal Newton methods can recover tensor-method complexity without tensors, offering a practical route to second-order stationary points in nonconvex optimization.

title: Minimax Rates For Robust Gaussian Mean Estimation Near The Breakdown Point Under Constraints
authors: Matey Neykov Tuorui Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the mean estimation of Gaussian location model with star-shaped constraints under adversarial contamination, where at most [MATH] among [MATH] observations are corrupted by an oracle adversary. We characterize the minimax squared [MATH] risk throughout the full range of contamination level [MATH]. The minimax risk is \asymp \big( \delta _\varepsilon ^{*2} \vee \sigma ^2\varepsilon ^2\log {1-2\varepsilon } \big) \wedge d^2 , where [MATH], [MATH] is the local entropy of constraint set [MATH], [MATH] is the diameter of [MATH] (set [MATH] if [MATH] is unbounded), [MATH] is the covariance of the Gaussian noise, and [MATH] is a sufficiently large constant. Our result sheds light on the interaction between contamination error and information theoretic complexity in the regime of proximity to the breakdown point [MATH].
tldr: The paper establishes minimax rates for robust Gaussian mean estimation under star-shaped constraints with adversarial contamination approaching the breakdown point.
motivation: Robust mean estimation is fundamental in high-dimensional statistics, but sharp minimax behavior near the breakdown point under structural constraints is not fully characterized.
