conclusion: Attack history serves both repair and reuse, motivating disclosure policies such as describing a technique without the full attack text.

title: FIDES-Live: Evaluating Behavioral Concordance In Sequential Trading Agents
authors: Arther Tian, Alex Ding, Simon Wu, Aaron Chan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential trading agents produce decisions, orders, execution receipts, account states, and reports that need not agree, even when the final portfolio value is correctly computed. We present FIDES-Live, an operational extension of FIDES from generated strategy concordance to the audit of sequential agent traces. The protocol separates structured decision validity, optional numerical commitment adherence, execution and ledger reconciliation, and receipt- grounded reporting, with explicit coverage and unscorable outcomes. We retrospectively audit ten requested inference routes over 7,299 cryptocurrency account-rounds and a 310-round equity pilot, using real market observations and local paper execution. Cryptocurrency decision validity is 97.35% and structured reporting accuracy is 90.81% among scorable responses, but route-level decision and reporting performance can diverge sharply. Commitment adherence is 94.36% overall; it falls to 62.63% on constraints emitted with nonempty order proposals, compared with 97.56% for valid empty proposals. All retained cash and position transitions reconcile with recorded fills, while execution controls and unavailable quotes explain separate rejection populations. Short-window marked returns provide descriptive context rather than a new test of whether concordance predicts alpha. These observations motivate reporting concordance, evidence coverage, activity, and financial outcomes separately. They do not establish long-run trading skill, semantic faithfulness of explanations, or causal benefits from audit feedback.
tldr: FIDES-Live is an auditing protocol that checks whether sequential LLM trading agents' decisions, orders, execution receipts, and reports agree with each other across 7,299 cryptocurrency account-rounds and a 310-round equity pilot.
motivation: Sequential trading agents can produce internally inconsistent artifacts—decisions, orders, ledger states, and narrative reports—even when final portfolio values are computed correctly, so an operational audit layer is needed to detect such divergences.
method: The protocol decomposes agent traces into structured decision validity, optional numerical commitment adherence, execution/ledger reconciliation, and receipt-grounded reporting, with explicit coverage and unscorable categories; it is applied retrospectively to ten inference routes using real market observations and local paper execution.
result: Decision validity is 97.35% and structured reporting accuracy 90.81% among scorable responses, commitment adherence is 94.36% overall but drops to 62.63% for constraints emitted alongside nonempty order proposals; all cash and position transitions reconcile with recorded fills.
conclusion: Reporting concordance, evidence coverage, activity, and financial outcomes should be reported separately; the study does not establish long-run trading skill, semantic faithfulness of explanations, or causal benefits of audit feedback.

title: Counting By The Book: Verifying Alaska's Ranked-Choice Elections
authors: Lucy Horowitz
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Alaska's ranked-choice elections as a case study in Formally Verified Democracy, a program to establish election results through formally checked proofs. We formalize an interpretation of Alaska's tabulation rules in Lean, verify its implementation, and prove election-specific results. Across 115 ranked-choice contests in Alaska since 2022, we identify 75 ballot records across 10 contests that were counted differently from this interpretation by a program reproducing the published results, without changing any winners. We trace these differences to overvotes and duplicate rankings and examine their legal justification, showing how formal verification can expose consequential choices in translating election law into software.
tldr: The paper formalizes Alaska's ranked-choice election tabulation rules in Lean, verifies an implementation against them, and audits discrepancies in 115 contests since 2022.
motivation: Election results are increasingly produced by complex software, yet there is little formally checked grounding for how tabulation rules are translated into code, creating risk of consequential but unnoticed interpretive choices.
method: The authors encode an interpretation of Alaska's ranked-choice tabulation rules in the Lean proof assistant, verify an implementation against that specification, and compare with a program reproducing published results across 115 contests.
result: They find 75 ballot records in 10 contests counted differently from their formal interpretation, attributable to overvotes and duplicate rankings, though no contest winner changes.
conclusion: Formal verification can expose legally consequential ambiguities in translating election law into software, offering a template for 'Formally Verified Democracy'.

title: Peak-DNA: Recurrent Morphology In Global Narrative Propagation
authors: Joosung Kim, Luyonghe Li, Shanwen Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global narrative streams exhibit noisy, fragmented, and asynchronous amplification bursts, making direct waveform comparison unreliable for recurrence analysis. This paper introduces Peak-DNA, a framework for identifying recurrent propagation morphology in global narrative streams. The proposed framework transforms hourly GDELT activity into normalized macro-peak episodes through denoising, macro-peak consolidation, and temporal alignment, and compares propagation morphology using DTW-based similarity analysis. Using GDELT narrative streams, we analyze five high-amplification narrative domains: Iran, Defense, AI, Space/Elon, and Quantum/PQC. The results show that amplification events repeatedly converge toward morphology-level propagation patterns within each narrative domain. DTW-based similarity analysis further demonstrates strong intra-domain structural compactness despite heterogeneous publication dynamics and severe observational noise. These findings suggest a measurable morphology layer beyond semantic content or anomaly intensity, providing an initial structural foundation for recurrence-aware narrative monitoring, propagation family discovery, and longitudinal Narrative Genome analysis.
tldr: Peak-DNA is a data-driven framework that identifies recurrent propagation morphologies in global narrative streams derived from GDELT hourly activity, using denoising, macro-peak consolidation, and DTW-based similarity analysis.
motivation: Global narrative amplification bursts are noisy, fragmented, and asynchronous, so direct waveform comparison is unreliable; the authors seek a stable 'morphology layer' that captures how narratives propagate beyond semantic content or raw anomaly intensity.
method: Hourly GDELT activity is transformed into normalized macro-peak episodes via denoising, peak consolidation, and temporal alignment, then compared across five narrative domains (Iran, Defense, AI, Space/Elon, Quantum/PQC) using dynamic time warping similarity.
result: Amplification events repeatedly converge to domain-specific morphology patterns, with strong intra-domain structural compactness despite heterogeneous publication dynamics and heavy observational noise.
conclusion: The authors argue for a measurable morphology layer enabling recurrence-aware narrative monitoring, propagation family discovery, and longitudinal 'Narrative Genome' analysis; the work has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimality And Impossibility In Multidimensional Strategyproof Facility Location
authors: Jianan Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study facility location in multidimensional normed spaces with the objective of minimizing social cost, the sum of agents' distances to their nearest facility. A deterministic mechanism selects [MATH] facility locations based on the reports of [MATH] agents and is strategyproof (SP) if no agent can reduce her distance by misreporting her location. We establish optimal approximation ratios and impossibility results. For a single facility in the Euclidean plane, we prove that the optimal approximation ratios among deterministic SP mechanisms are exactly those obtained by Goel and Hann-Caruthers [SCW 2023] for the coordinate-wise median (CM): [MATH] for odd [MATH] and [MATH] for even [MATH]. We remove the anonymity assumption from their optimality result. However, CM is not always optimal in non-Euclidean spaces: we give an SP mechanism that minimizes social cost exactly in [MATH], whereas CM has a tight uniform approximation ratio of [MATH] already in the plane. We then consider two facilities in [MATH] spaces with [MATH] and prove two impossibility results for every [MATH]. In the plane, no deterministic SP mechanism has a finite approximation ratio. In higher dimensions, the same impossibility holds for anonymous deterministic SP mechanisms. Finally, a reduction using distant agents and a limiting argument extends both impossibility results to every [MATH] with [MATH].
tldr: The paper derives optimal approximation ratios and impossibility results for strategyproof deterministic facility location mechanisms in multidimensional normed spaces.
motivation: Facility location under social cost is a canonical mechanism design problem, and the extent to which strategyproofness degrades efficiency in multidimensional and non-Euclidean settings was not fully characterized.
method: The author proves tight approximation bounds for the coordinate-wise median mechanism, constructs an exactly optimal SP mechanism in L1 spaces, and establishes impossibility results for two facilities using distant-agent reductions and limiting arguments.
result: Coordinate-wise median is shown optimal for a single facility in the Euclidean plane without anonymity assumptions, L1 admits an exactly optimal SP mechanism, and no deterministic SP mechanism attains a finite approximation ratio for two facilities in the plane, with extensions to general Lp spaces.
conclusion: Strategyproofness imposes severe efficiency limits in multidimensional facility location, and the structure of the normed space qualitatively changes what is achievable.

title: Measuring Users' Security And Privacy Concerns About Third-Party Community Bots On Discord
authors: Tu Le Kofi Ampomah
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third-party community-based bots are central to how social platforms such as Discord work. They moderate content, manage roles, play music, and support AI-assisted conversations across millions of servers. Yet when a bot is installed in a server, it can access messages, user profiles, and server metadata concerning members who did not participate in the installation decision, with no standardized way to communicate the associated security and privacy implications. In this paper, we analyze 23,102 third-party Discord bots and 183,142 user reviews spanning 49 detected languages and five years of feedback (2021-2026). We employ LLM-based knowledge distillation and fine-tune a DeBERTa-based classifier to identify candidate security and privacy (S&P)-relevant reviews. After manually validating the complete classifier-positive set, we retain 8,832 reviews identified as S&P-relevant, representing an observed pipeline yield of 4.82%, and map them to a 31-theme S&P taxonomy extending prior work. Our results show that S&P-related reviews focus heavily on Data Sharing (30.5%) and Data Collection (16.2%). Confession and anonymity bots have pipeline-identified SPRRs above 50%, more than ten times the ecosystem-wide pipeline yield of 4.82%. Star ratings may obscure the frequency and valence of S&P-related discussion, while conventional metadata features, such as permission count and administrator status, show only weak associations with user-reported S&P concerns. We then build BotLens, a proof-of-concept auditing framework that combines review-derived S&P signals with bot metadata to provide on-demand decision support for the community-based bot ecosystem. BotLens exposes six tools through a Model Context Protocol server, supporting bot-level checkups, server-wide comparison, and integration with AI agents.
tldr: A large-scale measurement study of 23,102 third-party Discord bots and 183,142 user reviews to characterize users' security and privacy concerns, culminating in a proof-of-concept auditing framework called BotLens.
motivation: Third-party community bots on platforms like Discord can access messages, profiles, and server metadata of users who never consented to their installation, and there is no standardized way to communicate the resulting security and privacy implications.
method: The authors scrape bot listings and reviews across 49 languages and five years, use LLM-based knowledge distillation to fine-tune a DeBERTa classifier for security/privacy-relevant reviews, manually validate the classifier-positive set, and map it onto a 31-theme taxonomy; they then build BotLens, an MCP-server-based auditing tool combining review signals with bot metadata.
result: 8,832 S&P-relevant reviews (4.82% pipeline yield) were retained; discussion concentrates on data sharing (30.5%) and data collection (16.2%), confession and anonymity bots exceed 50% relevance, star ratings obscure S&P discussion, and conventional metadata such as permission count shows only weak association with concerns.
conclusion: User-reported security and privacy signals complement bot metadata and can support decision-making in community-bot ecosystems, motivating tools like BotLens for on-demand auditing.

title: Sybil-Proofness Of Generalized Adaptive Clinching And Implications For Blockchain Mechanism Design
authors: Chengkai Zhang, Yuhao Li, Elaine Shi, Mengqian Zhang, Lirong Xia, Qishen Han
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The adaptive clinching auction of Dobzinski, Lavi, and Nisan (FOCS'08) is a cornerstone of mechanism design with budget-constrained bidders, and it has since inspired a broad range of extensions to substantially richer market settings. Adaptive clinching enjoys compelling guarantees: it is Pareto optimal, and truthful bidding is a dominant strategy whenever budgets cannot be overreported. In many real-world environments, however, identities are cheap to create, making resilience to Sybil attacks an additional requirement. Whether the guarantees of adaptive clinching survive when a bidder can split its budget across fake identities has remained open. We introduce a generalized framework for adaptive clinching and prove that it satisfies Sybil-robust incentive compatibility: a bidder cannot benefit from splitting into any finite number of identities with arbitrary value reports, provided their aggregate reported budget does not exceed the bidder's enforceable true budget. Sybil resilience thus joins the list of ideal properties of adaptive clinching. Our work is motivated by practical problems in decentralized finance, where automated market makers (AMMs) are among the most widely used applications. We design a new AMM mechanism that extends classical adaptive clinching in two ways: it supports a two-sided market and protects against two-sided strategies, and it allows the supply function to depend on the auction state. Its one-sided special case is captured by our generalized adaptive clinching framework, and our proof techniques show that the full two-sided mechanism simultaneously satisfies Sybil-robust incentive compatibility and a relaxed notion of Pareto optimality. We argue that these guarantees are essentially the best possible via impossibility results. More broadly, our work reveals new connections between classical algorithmic game theory and modern decentralized blockchains.
tldr: The paper proves Sybil-robust incentive compatibility for a generalized adaptive clinching auction and applies it to a decentralized-finance automated market maker design.
motivation: Adaptive clinching auctions have strong guarantees, but whether they remain resilient when bidders can split budgets across fake identities was open, and this matters for blockchain/DeFi mechanism design.
method: The authors introduce a generalized adaptive clinching framework and prove Sybil-robust incentive compatibility; they also design a two-sided AMM mechanism with state-dependent supply and prove Sybil-robustness and relaxed Pareto optimality.
result: They show that a bidder cannot benefit by splitting into finitely many identities with arbitrary value reports as long as aggregate reported budget does not exceed enforceable true budget, and provide impossibility results suggesting the guarantees are essentially optimal.
conclusion: Sybil resilience is added to the ideal properties of adaptive clinching, revealing connections between algorithmic game theory and decentralized blockchain mechanism design.

title: An Empirical Study Of Undisclosed Charges In Hook-Based Decentralized Exchanges
authors: Kai Ma, Tianle Sun, Shun Zhou, Boyao Yang, Ningyu He, Haoyu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many decentralized exchanges use automated market makers (AMMs) to trade assets against liquidity pools. Modern AMMs allow third-party contracts, called Hooks, to customize this process. However, Hooks can impose additional deductions that fee breakdowns based on standard pool parameters do not itemize. We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale empirical study of the production Hook ecosystem, focusing on these undisclosed settlement charges. Our study covers 7,873 Hook deployments, 50,011 pools, and 296M pool events on Uniswap v4 and PancakeSwap Infinity across Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain (BSC) through August 1, 2026. We develop a bytecode analysis that reconstructs how Hooks change traders' payments and receipts, separating charges from exchanged assets and standard fees. We then reconstruct historical settlements to measure charging frequency and economic burden. We find that direct settlement adjustment is the dominant Hook capability, supported by 71.37% of registered Hooks. Charging capability is widespread and often exercised: 24.30% of Hooks can impose undisclosed deductions, and these deductions occur in 59.23% of accounted swaps involving such Hooks. These charges generate millions of dollars in revenue, with $3.97M recorded across Hooks with available token prices. These findings reveal a gap between standard fee displays and actual trading costs, motivating explicit disclosure of Hook deductions alongside standard fees.
tldr: A large-scale empirical measurement study of undisclosed settlement charges imposed by Hooks in Uniswap v4 and PancakeSwap Infinity AMM deployments on Ethereum and BSC.
motivation: Modern AMM-based decentralized exchanges let third-party Hook contracts customize pool behavior, which can introduce extra deductions that standard fee breakdowns do not itemize, creating a hidden cost gap for traders.
method: The authors perform bytecode analysis to reconstruct how Hooks alter traders' payments and receipts, separating Hook charges from exchanged assets and standard fees, then replay 296M pool events across 7,873 Hook deployments and 50,011 pools to quantify charging frequency and economic burden.
result: Direct settlement adjustment is the dominant Hook capability (71.37% of registered Hooks), 24.30% of Hooks can impose undisclosed deductions, and these deductions occur in 59.23% of accounted swaps involving such Hooks, generating at least $3.97M in measured revenue.
conclusion: There is a measurable gap between displayed fees and actual trading costs, motivating explicit disclosure of Hook deductions alongside standard pool fees.

title: An Algebra Of Transformers
authors: Yong Wang, Zhiyan Wang, Hexiao Kang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On the theoretic analyses on transforms, they mainly focus on the computability analysis, such the Turing-completeness of unbounded precision transformers, the advantage of parallelizability of unbounded precision transformers and the limitations of bounded precision transformers. This paper give transformers an algebra for reasoning, which relies heavily on the functional decomposition results of transformers. This algebra uses functional decompositions as atomic actions, includes sequential composition and parallel composition, recursion for feedback and abstraction for hidden layers. As we know, it is the first attempt to model transformers logically and can be used to verify the correctness of transformer based applications.
tldr: The paper proposes a formal algebra for transformers built on functional decomposition, with sequential/parallel composition, recursion, and abstraction operators, intended for logical reasoning about and verification of transformer-based applications.
motivation: Existing theoretical work on transformers focuses on computability and expressivity (Turing-completeness of unbounded-precision models, limitations of bounded-precision models); the authors argue there is no logical/algebraic framework for compositional reasoning about transformer behaviour.
method: Transformers are decomposed into functional components which are treated as atomic actions, and an algebra is constructed by adding sequential composition, parallel composition, recursion (for feedback) and abstraction (for hidden layers).
result: The paper claims the first attempt at an algebraic/logical modelling of transformers, yielding a formalism usable for verifying correctness of transformer-based applications.
conclusion: The algebra provides a systematic logical foundation for reasoning about transformer architectures, though the emphasis is on classical computability and program verification rather than on any quantum or information-theoretic property.

title: What We Could Lose By Trying To Make Mars Habitable
authors: Ari Koeppel, Lonneke Roelofs, Santiago Vrech, Alicia M. Rutledge, Martin Turbet
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent push to develop Mars terraforming technologies, increasingly driven by unaccountable private wealth, risks the irreversible destruction of planetary records we have barely begun to read. In this sense, terraforming Mars would be akin to the destruction of the Library of Alexandria. Echoing Carl Sagan's words about the library, in this piece we argue that we should not let such an extensive loss of information happen again. As terraforming Mars would melt and destroy the icy record on Mars, we suggest closing an important gap in the COSPAR planetary protection framework, by expanding regulations on preventing biological contamination to preventing large-scale atmospheric modification and destruction of cryospheric and geologic records.
tldr: An opinion piece arguing that Mars terraforming would irreversibly destroy planetary records and cryospheric/geologic information, and that COSPAR planetary protection rules should be expanded to prevent large-scale atmospheric modification.
motivation: Growing privately funded interest in Mars terraforming threatens to melt and erase the Martian icy record before it can be studied, an irreversible loss comparable to the burning of the Library of Alexandria.
method: Policy and ethical argumentation grounded in planetary science, invoking Carl Sagan's reasoning and proposing an extension of the COSPAR planetary protection framework from biological contamination to atmospheric and cryospheric/geologic record preservation.
result: The authors identify a regulatory gap: current planetary protection rules do not cover large-scale atmospheric modification or destruction of cryospheric and geologic records.
conclusion: Terraforming should be constrained by expanded planetary-protection regulations to avoid an extensive, irreversible loss of scientific information.

title: Efficient Regime Boundary Detection In Discontinuous Simulation Models
authors: Federico Betti, Eleni Chatzi, Paolo Tiso
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many computational models exhibit multiple operating regimes separated by abrupt or non-smooth transitions as the input parameters vary. Such regime transitions complicate the construction of global parametric reduced-order models, often necessitating large training datasets to capture the distinct system behaviors. Accurate regime boundary detection instead enables localized modeling strategies by partitioning the parameter space into regions of qualitatively distinct behavior. In many cases, regime switching corresponds to the excursion set of a simulator output. When such a quantity is discontinuous or non-smooth, regression-based algorithms for level set estimation can struggle to correctly approximate the boundary. In this work, we show that solving a resulting binary classification problem can improve sample efficiency and we further propose a novel adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines. Unlike uncertainty-based sampling schemes, the proposed approach uses a continuous search space and efficiently explores the currently estimated boundary in its tangential directions by gradient-based dynamic sampling. Because the decision function admits analytical gradients, this exploration incurs negligible computational overhead relative to the underlying model evaluations. Then, a space-filling subset of the generated samples is selected as the next batch to be queried. We demonstrate improved sample efficiency compared to existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples. The proposed method provides a sample-efficient framework for regime boundary detection in a broad class of discontinuous simulation-driven problems.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines to detect regime boundaries in discontinuous simulation models more sample-efficiently.
motivation: Regime transitions in parametric computational models hinder global reduced-order modeling, and regression-based level set estimation struggles when simulator outputs are discontinuous or non-smooth.
method: The authors formulate regime boundary detection as binary classification, use support vector machines with analytical gradients for boundary exploration, and introduce a gradient-based dynamic sampling strategy followed by space-filling batch selection.
result: The proposed method improves sample efficiency compared with existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples.
conclusion: The framework provides a sample-efficient approach to regime boundary detection in discontinuous simulation-driven problems, enabling localized modeling strategies.

title: Activity-based Temporal Hypergraphs: From Individual Activity To Collective Social Dynamics
authors: Marco Mancastroppa, Giulia Cencetti, Iacopo Iacopini, Giovanni Petri, Alain Barrat
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal hypergraphs provide an interesting representation for many social systems, as they integrate both the temporal and group nature of social interactions. Designing models of time-varying hyper-networks yields thus a convenient way to generate surrogates of empirical social systems, to understand the mechanisms underlying their emergent properties, and to investigate the evolution of dynamical processes taking place on such structures. Here, we focus on a specific and powerful class of these models, the activity-based temporal hypergraphs. We show how activity mechanisms provide control over the time scale of the dynamics, allow high modelling flexibility, and capture heterogeneity in agents' behavior. We also highlight how the activity can straightforwardly be extracted from empirical data to create surrogate datasets. We present paradigmatic examples of such models: the higher-order activity-driven models (HADx), which show that different underlying rules for the selection of active interactions produce different higher-order dynamics; the Emerging Activity Temporal Hypergraph model (EATH), able to generate surrogates of empirical systems by using higher-order mechanisms driven by both activity and group memory. We conclude discussing future perspectives for activity-based temporal hypergraphs, highlighting the potential of this framework to bridge realistic modelling of social dynamics with the study of the complex dynamical process they can support, from social contagion to opinion dynamics.
tldr: The paper develops activity-based temporal hypergraph models to generate surrogates of empirical social systems and study collective social dynamics.
motivation: Temporal hypergraphs capture both the temporal and group nature of social interactions, and activity-based models offer flexible ways to model time-varying higher-order networks and their emergent dynamics.
method: The authors present and analyze activity-based temporal hypergraph frameworks, including higher-order activity-driven models (HADx) and the Emerging Activity Temporal Hypergraph (EATH) model, extracting activity from empirical data to construct surrogates.
result: They show that different rules for selecting active higher-order interactions produce different higher-order dynamics, and that EATH can generate surrogates of empirical systems using activity and group memory.
conclusion: Activity-based temporal hypergraphs provide a powerful framework for bridging realistic social modelling with the study of complex dynamical processes such as social contagion and opinion dynamics.

title: High-Efficiency Graphene Oxide Moir\'e Lenses Enabled By Cyclic Self-Assembly And Laser Nanoprinting
authors: Guiyuan Cao, Xinyuan Du, Han Lin, Baohua Jia, Shibiao Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moir\'e lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. The measured focusing efficiencies of individual GO lenses increase from 22.4% for two phase levels to 54.8% for six levels. Using this six-level modulation strategy, the fabricated GO Moir\'e lens achieves continuous focal-length tuning from approximately 10 to 90 mm. Full-colour imaging with magnifications ranging from 1X to 9X is experimentally demonstrated. These results establish a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy for efficient multilevel GO flat optics and demonstrate its potential for compact, reconfigurable imaging.
tldr: The paper demonstrates graphene oxide Moiré flat lenses fabricated by cyclic self-assembly and femtosecond laser nanoprinting, achieving improved focusing efficiency and continuous focal-length tuning for compact imaging.
motivation: Compact tunable-focus optical systems are desirable for imaging and machine vision, but existing metasurface Moiré lenses require complex nanofabrication that hinders large-area production.
method: The authors combine layer-by-layer self-assembly of graphene oxide and PDDA with spatially selective femtosecond laser ablation to construct multilevel phase profiles with atomic-scale thickness control.
result: Focusing efficiency increases from 22.4% with two phase levels to 54.8% with six levels, enabling continuous focal-length tuning from about 10 to 90 mm and full-colour imaging with 1X to 9X magnification.
conclusion: The cyclic mask-free fabrication strategy enables efficient multilevel graphene oxide flat optics and shows potential for compact reconfigurable imaging systems.

title: Cost Benefits Of Designing Carbon Capture Processes For Part-load Operation Of Power Plants
authors: David Yang Shu, Boxun Huang, Yurim Kim, Rahul Gandhi, Randall Field, Sungho Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As fossil power plants increasingly cycle to balance variable renewable generation, carbon capture plants must be designed for a wide range of part-load operating conditions, to avoid excessive capital costs. However, accounting for the variability in design optimization yields higher computational complexity, and is therefore not a current design methodology. Here, we apply two-stage stochastic optimization to identify optimal carbon capture plant designs accounting for part-load flue gas conditions. We reduce computational complexity through a data-driven approach-to-equilibrium model of the absorption and desorption processes. Operating scenarios are derived from real-world part-load operation data of coal and natural gas combined cycle power plants. Our results demonstrate that designs optimized over multiple operating scenarios substantially reduce equipment sizes, lowering capital costs by 5-9 % at the expense of higher operating costs, resulting in a moderate reduction in total annualized cost by 0.5-1.6 %. The lowest costs are achieved when targeting an average capture target across operating scenarios, which allows CO2 capture to be shifted from full-load to part-load periods to reduce peak equipment sizes without compromising overall CO2 emission reductions. These cost benefits are robust across sensitivity analyses and increase with higher shares of part-load operation. Thus, part-load variability should be considered at the design stage, particularly for plants subject to variable load.
tldr: This paper uses two-stage stochastic optimization and a data-driven equilibrium model to design carbon capture plants that account for part-load power plant operation, finding modest total cost reductions and lower capital costs.
motivation: Fossil power plants increasingly cycle to balance variable renewable generation, so carbon capture plants must be designed for variable part-load conditions rather than only full-load operation to avoid excessive capital costs.
method: The authors apply two-stage stochastic optimization with operating scenarios derived from real part-load data of coal and natural gas combined cycle plants, reducing complexity via a data-driven approach-to-equilibrium model of absorption and desorption.
result: Optimized designs reduce equipment sizes and capital costs by 5-9% at the expense of higher operating costs, yielding a moderate 0.5-1.6% reduction in total annualized cost; targeting an average capture rate across scenarios performs best.
conclusion: Part-load variability should be considered at the design stage for carbon capture plants, especially under high shares of variable operation, though the cost benefits are moderate.

title: Boundary And Interior Of Root Sets Of Power Series
authors: Jacob Kewarth
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the set [MATH] of roots of power series with coefficients in [MATH] and constant coefficient [MATH]. We prove that every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of this form is an interior point of [MATH]. Moreover we establish a dimension formula and show the corresponding Hausdorff measure is finite and positive for a family of attractors parameterized by boundary parameters [MATH]. Finally we show that [MATH] has Lebesgue measure zero.
tldr: The paper studies the set of roots of power series with prescribed coefficient domain and constant term, proving interior-point, dimension, Hausdorff measure, and measure-zero properties.
motivation: It aims to characterize the geometry and measure of root sets arising from power series/polynomial families.
method: The work uses complex-analytic and fractal-geometric techniques, including dimension formulas and Hausdorff measure estimates for parameterized attractors.
result: Every nonreal root in the unit disk is shown to be an interior point of the root set; a dimension formula is established with finite positive Hausdorff measure for a family of attractors, and the full root set has Lebesgue measure zero.
conclusion: The root sets have rich geometric structure but are measure-zero, with interior behavior near nonreal unit-disk roots and fractal-dimensional boundary families.

title: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn Llm Jailbreaks Via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
authors: Junle Li, Siqi Chen, Jiakai Li, Bingzhuo Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-turn jailbreaks turn dialogue safety into a trace property: a violation may become identifiable only when user intent and assistant behavior are considered across multiple turns. Existing guard models largely classify individual messages or exchanges and return risk scores or labels, without executable safety semantics or a formally checkable decision trail. We present SpecGuard, a training-free, specification-driven framework for monitoring multi-turn LLM interactions. SpecGuard uses a fixed atomic-proposition contract to map natural-language observations into causally scoped, evidence-backed facts, and expresses forbidden interaction patterns as Linear Temporal Logic specifications. Each specification is compiled into a symbolic finite automaton that incrementally consumes the resulting dialogue trace. The same monitoring mechanism supports buffered runtime checking and retrospective auditing, while accepting runs produce replayable witnesses that identify the triggered specification, supporting facts, and relevant dialogue turns. Experiments on multi-turn safety benchmarks show that SpecGuard consistently outperforms representative open-source guard models while maintaining controlled false-positive rates. These results demonstrate a practical path from heuristic risk classification toward formally specified, verifiable, and auditable LLM safety monitoring, without learned detector parameters or access to the protected model.
tldr: SpecGuard is a training-free, specification-driven runtime monitoring framework that detects multi-turn LLM jailbreaks by expressing forbidden interaction patterns as Linear Temporal Logic specifications compiled into symbolic finite automata over dialogue traces.
motivation: Multi-turn jailbreaks are trace properties that only become identifiable across several turns, yet existing guard models classify single messages or exchanges without executable safety semantics or a formally checkable decision trail.
method: The framework uses a fixed atomic-proposition contract to map natural-language observations into causally scoped, evidence-backed facts, expresses forbidden patterns as LTL specifications, and compiles each into a symbolic finite automaton that incrementally consumes the dialogue trace, supporting both buffered runtime checking and retrospective auditing with replayable witnesses.
result: Experiments on multi-turn safety benchmarks show SpecGuard consistently outperforms representative open-source guard models while maintaining controlled false-positive rates, without learned detector parameters or access to the protected model.
conclusion: The work offers a practical path from heuristic risk classification toward formally specified, verifiable, and auditable LLM safety monitoring.

title: Silent Blindness: Fault Vulnerability Of Hardware Malware Detectors
authors: Alireza Abolhasani Zeraatkar, Parnian Shabani Kamran, Parsa Mirfasihi, Saleh Khalaj Monfared, Hussain Al-Asaad
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware malware detectors (HMDs) classify hardware performance-counter measurements to identify malicious execution. Faults in their decision logic or parameters can weaken detection and allow malware to be classified as benign. We investigate this vulnerability through structural fault injection across a design space comprising 18 classifiers, four counter budgets, and AdaBoost and Bagging ensembles. The simulation evaluates 453,174 decision stuck-at and selected parameter bit-flip events on a 7,400-instance. Primary comparisons use 128 completed configurations. These completed-subset results are distinguished from the simulation summaries covering 140 configurations with enumerable fault sites. Fault outcomes are classified by their security consequences, including evasion, false-alarm increases, and metric silence. A fault is critical when malware recall decreases by at least five percentage points. Tree-based models exhibit a lower mean critical-fault fraction than function-based models, 5.3% versus 14.3%; exhaustive-only analysis preserves this ordering. Moreover, 72.3% of evaluated tree faults are metric-silent, changing both recall and false-positive rate by less than 0.1 percentage points without necessarily preserving individual predictions. Among the 27 completed matched comparisons, Bagging reduces criticality in 26, whereas AdaBoost increases it in two. Finally, an exact minimax selection method identifies protection candidates under additive unit costs and ideal correction. For a representative J48 detector, protecting 16 of 115 structural units reduces predicted maximum recall loss from 60.1 to 3.3 percentage points. These results characterize structural-model sensitivity and potential protection benefits; faulted RTL correspondence and physical hardening overhead remain unvalidated.
tldr: The paper studies how faults injected into hardware malware detectors' decision logic or parameters can degrade detection, letting malware be misclassified as benign, and proposes a minimax selection of structural units to protect.
motivation: Hardware performance-counter-based malware detectors are deployed as a security mechanism, but their robustness to internal faults in the classifier logic had not been systematically characterized.
method: Structural fault injection across 18 classifiers, four counter budgets, and AdaBoost/Bagging ensembles, simulating 453,174 stuck-at and parameter bit-flip events on a 7,400-instance dataset, with criticality defined as at least a 5 percentage-point drop in malware recall plus an exact minimax selection for protection.
result: Tree-based models show a lower mean critical-fault fraction than function-based models (5.3% vs 14.3%), 72.3% of evaluated tree faults are metric-silent, Bagging reduces criticality in 26 of 27 matched comparisons, and protecting 16 of 115 units in a J48 detector cuts predicted worst-case recall loss from 60.1 to 3.3 points.
conclusion: Structural sensitivity of HMD classifiers is quantified and protection candidates identified, though RTL correspondence of faults and physical hardening overhead remain unvalidated.

title: A Functional Model For Hyponormal Contractions
authors: Sachin Paramanik Amit Maji
abstract: ArXiv:2610.35880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical model for a class of hyponormal contractions [MATH] satisfying [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are the associated defect spaces for [MATH]. We also show that, under a certain condition, a contraction [MATH] with [MATH] is hyponormal.
tldr: The paper constructs a functional model for a class of hyponormal contractions and provides a sufficient condition for a contraction to be hyponormal.
motivation: The work aims to extend analytical model theory from contractions to hyponormal contractions using associated defect spaces.
method: It employs operator-theoretic techniques, including defect space analysis and functional model constructions for contractions.
result: An analytical model is established for hyponormal contractions satisfying a specified condition, and a condition is given under which a contraction is hyponormal.
conclusion: The results advance pure operator theory but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ultrafast Light-electron Modulation For Free-electron Quantum Optics: Fundamentals And Applications
authors: Zirui Zhao, Ruoyu Chen, Changying Li, Yongcheng Ding, Zhaopin Chen, Xinbing Song, Shuaishuai Sun, Ye Tian, Kangpeng Wang, Yiming Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.36182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherent optical modulation of free-electron wavepackets offers a route to ultrafast beam steering, energy exchange, temporal compression, and quantum-state shaping. Recent advances in photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect (KDE) and dielectric laser acceleration (DLA) have demonstrated strong light-electron coupling, but longitudinal energy modulation, transverse momentum transfer, and wavepacket-dependent diffraction are still commonly described with separate models. Here, we develop a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets. Within this framework, we identify longitudinal and transverse modulation channels, analogous to electro-optic phase modulation and acousto-optic diffraction of light, respectively, and show how their operation depends on wavepacket extent, recoil, phase matching, and optical-field geometry. This formulation organizes PINEM, Raman-Nath and Bragg diffraction, DLA-like acceleration, and anomalous PINEM as limiting regimes of a common modulation picture. The resulting framework provides design principles for free-electron modulators that can control energy spectra, temporal density, transverse wavefronts, and electron-photon quantum interfaces, establishing LEM as a device-level platform for programmable femtosecond-to-attosecond matter-wave control.
tldr: Analysis failed
